# Andong Travel Guide: Hahoe Village, Confucian Academies and Jjimdak

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/andong-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-30

## Quick answer

- Andong is where you see old Korea's clan villages and Confucian academies. Sites in Andong belong to three UNESCO listings: Hahoe Village (2010), Dosan and Byeongsan Seowon (2019) and Bongjeongsa Temple (2018).
- Hahoe Village costs ₩5,000 for adults. Last entry is 16:30 from October to March and 17:30 from April to September, so don't arrive late in the afternoon.
- Get there by KTX-Eum from Seoul Station, Cheongnyangni or (on selected trains) Sangbong to Andong Station. Journey times depend on the departure station, so check your train when booking, then take bus 210 or Express 2 to Hahoe.

**Andong, reached from Seoul by KTX-Eum, is the place to see a living clan village and the Confucian academies of the Joseon era: sites here belong to three UNESCO World Heritage listings.** Start with Hahoe Village (adults ₩5,000; last entry 16:30 from October to March), the Hahoe mask dance show at 14:00 (Tuesday to Sunday from March to December, Saturdays and Sundays in January and February) and a plate of Andong jjimdak, a braised chicken dish born in the city's old market.

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1324), [Andong Hahoe Village](http://www.hahoe.or.kr/coding/sub5/sub3.asp) (Korean), [Hahoe mask dance society](http://www.hahoemask.co.kr/) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438); checked Oct 30, 2026.

![Graphic: Andong at a glance — UNESCO sites, Hahoe Village fees and last entry, the mask dance show, KTX-Eum from Seoul and buses to Hahoe](/img/andong-steps.png?v=5a50cd0e "Andong at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Why go | Hahoe, a clan village still lived in, and Joseon-era Confucian academies (seowon) |
| UNESCO | Hahoe Village (2010) · Dosan and Byeongsan Seowon (2019) · Bongjeongsa Temple (2018) |
| Getting there | KTX-Eum from Seoul Station, Cheongnyangni or (selected trains) Sangbong to Andong Station; journey times differ by departure station |
| Top sights | Hahoe Village and its mask dance · Byeongsan Seowon · Dosan Seowon · Woryeonggyo Bridge at night |
| Eat | Andong jjimdak · salted mackerel (gangodeungeo) · heotjesatbap |
| Day trip or overnight? | A day covers Hahoe, Byeongsan and Woryeonggyo; stay a night to add Dosan Seowon and Bongjeongsa, KTO says |

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1324) and [Korea Tourism Organization — Andong](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Why Andong matters

UNESCO describes Hahoe and its sister village Yangdong as "the two most representative historic, clan villages in Korea," founded in the 14th–15th century. Andong's sites are part of three World Heritage listings:

| UNESCO listing | Inscribed | Andong's part in it |
|---|---|---|
| **Historic Villages of Korea: Hahoe and Yangdong** | 2010 | Hahoe Village |
| **Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies** | 2019 | Dosan Seowon and Byeongsan Seowon, two of the nine academies |
| **Sansa, Buddhist Mountain Monasteries in Korea** | 2018 | Bongjeongsa Temple, one of the seven monasteries |

Source: UNESCO — [Hahoe and Yangdong](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1324), [Seowon](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1498) and [Sansa](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1562); locations from the [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438) and [Andong City](https://www.andong.go.kr/dosanseowon/main.do) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Hahoe Village

![A river bend with sandbanks and pine trees, and the roofs of Hahoe Village beyond, with hills behind](/img/photo-andong-hahoe-river.jpg?v=b3ee6914 "Hahoe Folk Village by the Nakdonggang River, October 2022. Photo: Bernard Gagnon (CC0), cropped.")

The Nakdonggang River wraps around Hahoe, and the Ryu clan of Pungsan still makes up 70 percent of the villagers, the Korea Tourism Organization says. UNESCO notes the clusters of one-storey, mud-walled, thatched-roof houses that were "formerly for commoners." A full walk takes about 1 to 1.5 hours.

| | |
|---|---|
| Admission | Adults (19–64) ₩5,000 · teenagers (13–18) ₩2,500 · children (7–12) ₩1,500 |
| Last entry | 16:30 from October to March · 17:30 from April to September |
| Free extras | Parking, the shuttle bus and the Hahoe World Mask Museum |
| Closed | Open year-round |
| View | Buyongdae Cliff, across the river, gives a panoramic view of the village (KTO) |

Source: [Andong Hahoe Village — visitor information](http://www.hahoe.or.kr/coding/sub5/sub3.asp) (Korean), [Korea Tourism Organization — Hahoe Village](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=111087) and [Andong Tourism](https://www.tourandong.com/public/sub5/sub2_2.cshtml) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Hahoe's free admission for people aged 65 and over applies to Korean nationals, the village's own fee table says, so older foreign visitors should ask at the ticket office which fare applies.

![Tile and thatched roofs of Hahoe Village seen from above among trees](/img/photo-andong-hahoe-rooftops.jpg?v=0d63cccf "Rooftops of Hahoe Folk Village, October 2022. Photo: Bernard Gagnon (CC0), cropped.")

### The Hahoe mask dance show

Hahoe Byeolsingut Tallori, a mask dance drama performed in carved wooden Hahoe masks, is a National Intangible Cultural Heritage (designated 1980). The preservation society stages a regular one-hour show at the village's mask dance theater:

| Months | Days | Time |
|---|---|---|
| March to December | Tuesday to Sunday | 14:00–15:00 |
| January and February | Saturday and Sunday | 14:00–15:00 |

Source: [Hahoe Byeolsingut Tallori Preservation Society](http://www.hahoemask.co.kr/) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** The 14:00 mask dance runs Tuesday to Sunday from March to December and on Saturdays and Sundays in January and February, once a day, so build your Hahoe visit around it. Check the society's current schedule before you go.

![A thatched-roof house with mud walls and latticed doors under a clear sky](/img/photo-andong-hahoe-thatched.jpg?v=fd4c7032 "A thatched house in Hahoe Folk Village, October 2022. Photo: Bernard Gagnon (CC0), cropped.")

### Seonyu Julbul Nori

Hahoe also holds Seonyu Julbul Nori on select Saturday nights. The published 2026 schedule lists selected Saturdays in May and August–October, ending on October 31. For future visits, check the organizer's newly announced dates and ticket rules; don't assume the 2026 booking arrangements will apply in 2027.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Andong](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438) and [Andong Hahoe Village notices](http://www.hahoe.or.kr/) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## The Confucian academies and Bongjeongsa

| | Byeongsan Seowon | Dosan Seowon | Bongjeongsa Temple |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | Academy moved here in 1572 by the scholar Yu Seong-nyong and renamed in 1614, facing the Nakdonggang River | Academy built in 1574 to honor the scholar Toegye Yi Hwang | Mountain temple; its Geungnakjeon Hall is considered Korea's oldest surviving wooden building (KTO) |
| Hours | 09:00–18:00 (March–October) · 09:00–17:00 (November–February) | 09:00–18:00, last entry 17:30 (February–October) · 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:30 (November–January) | 07:00–19:00 (March–October) · 08:00–17:00 (November–February) |
| Admission | Not listed on the city's fee table: check on site | Adults ₩2,000 | Free |
| Bus | 210 | Express 3 or 512 (a few buses a day, about 45 minutes) | Express 2 or 310 |

Source: [Andong City — Dosan Seowon](https://www.andong.go.kr/dosanseowon/contents.do?mId=0502000000) (Korean), [Andong Tourism — fees and hours](https://www.tourandong.com/public/sub5/sub2_2.cshtml) (Korean), [Korea Tourism Organization — Byeongsanseowon](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=107434) and [Andong](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438); checked Oct 30, 2026.

The Korea Tourism Organization says free commentary in English, Japanese and Chinese is available at major attractions such as Hahoe Village and Dosan Seowon. For Hahoe, the village's tourist information and interpretation desk is on +82-54-840-3803.

## What to eat

| Dish | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Andong jjimdak** | Chicken braised with vegetables and seasoning. KTO says it was born in the chicken alley of Andong Old Market, which has had one since the 1970s; about 30 restaurants line what's now called Jjimdak Alley |
| **Salted mackerel (gangodeungeo)** | Andong is far inland, so locals traditionally salted mackerel to keep it fresh; often part of a set meal |
| **Heotjesatbap** | Bibimbap made with the same ingredients as ancestral-rite food, a dish tied to Andong's Confucian traditions |
| **Andong guksi** | Noodles made from wheat flour and soybean powder |
| **Andong soju** | A traditionally distilled local spirit; some is very strong (KTO says over 40% ABV), so check the label |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Jjimdak Alley](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=14987) and [Andong](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438), [Andong Tourism — food](https://www.tourandong.com/public/sub3/sub1.cshtml) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Traveling solo? Andong jjimdak usually comes as a whole chicken for two to three people, KTO says, while many restaurants serve a salted mackerel set meal for one.

## Getting there and around

| | |
|---|---|
| By train | KTX-Eum from Seoul Station, Cheongnyangni or (selected trains) Sangbong to Andong Station. Trains from Seoul Station take longer than those from Cheongnyangni, and Korail's timetable changes from Nov 1, 2026, so check your train's time and fare when you [book](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) |
| By express bus | From Dong Seoul Terminal (about 3 hours) or Seoul Express Bus Terminal (about 2 hr 40 min), per Andong Tourism |
| To Hahoe | Bus 210, Express 2, Pungcheon 2 or the Hahoe shuttle bus from the Andong Station and bus terminal area |
| Bus fare | ₩1,500 by transit card, with a free transfer within an hour if you tap off |
| Bus times | Few buses run on some routes: check the Andong Bus Information System (Korean) or [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Andong](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438), [Korail timetables](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (Korean) and [Andong Tourism — transport](https://www.tourandong.com/public/sub5/sub1_2.cshtml) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## A one-day plan

> **Our take:** This order puts Hahoe around the 14:00 show and keeps Woryeonggyo Bridge, lit up at night, for last. Bus times vary, so check them and pick one stop if time is short.

| Time | Where | Why then |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | KTX-Eum to Andong, bus to Hahoe | Allow time for the bus: some routes run infrequently |
| Midday | Hahoe Village and the 14:00 mask dance | The show is once a day |
| Afternoon | Byeongsan Seowon (bus 210) or Buyongdae | Check last-entry times |
| Evening | Jjimdak in the old market, then Woryeonggyo Bridge | The bridge is lit after dark |

## Before you go

1. Book your KTX-Eum and check the new timetable (from Nov 1, 2026).
2. Plan to reach Hahoe well before last entry (16:30 from October to March).
3. Catch the 14:00 mask dance show: Tuesday to Sunday from March to December; Saturdays and Sundays in January and February.
4. Check bus times on Naver Map or the Andong BIS: some routes run a few times a day.
5. Coming as a pair or group? Order a whole jjimdak to share.

Source: [Andong Hahoe Village](http://www.hahoe.or.kr/coding/sub5/sub3.asp) (Korean), [Hahoe mask dance society](http://www.hahoemask.co.kr/) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=1590438); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## FAQ

### Is Andong worth visiting?

In our view, yes, if you want old Korea beyond the palaces of Seoul: Hahoe is a clan village where people still live, and Andong's sites are part of three UNESCO World Heritage listings.

### How do I get from Seoul to Andong?

Take the KTX-Eum from Seoul Station, Cheongnyangni or (on selected trains) Sangbong to Andong Station. Journey times depend on the departure station; check your train's time and fare when booking, as Korail's timetable changes from Nov 1, 2026.

### How much is Hahoe Village?

Adults (19–64) pay ₩5,000, teenagers ₩2,500 and children ₩1,500. Last entry is 16:30 from October to March and 17:30 from April to September.

### When is the Hahoe mask dance performance?

At 14:00, Tuesday to Sunday from March to December, and on Saturdays and Sundays in January and February. There's no show on Mondays.

### Can you visit Andong in a day trip?

Yes for Hahoe Village, Byeongsan Seowon and Woryeonggyo Bridge, the Korea Tourism Organization says. Stay overnight if you also want Dosan Seowon and Bongjeongsa Temple.

# Gangneung Travel Guide: Ojukheon, Beaches, Coffee and Chodang Tofu

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/gangneung-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-30

## Quick answer

- Gangneung is an east-coast city of beaches, hanok estates and coffee. Start with Ojukheon, birthplace of the mother and son on Korea's 50,000- and 5,000-won notes (adults ₩3,000; last entry 17:00).
- Eat Chodang sundubu, soft tofu traditionally set with seawater, and try a coffee at Anmok Beach, where Gangneung's coffee culture started with vending machines.
- Get there by KTX-Eum: adult standard-class fares are ₩27,600 from Seoul Station or ₩26,000 from Cheongnyangni (Korail fare table as of Sep 1, 2026). These include a temporary discount that ends when faster running starts on the Cheongnyangni–Seowonju section.

**Gangneung, on Korea's east coast at the end of the KTX-Eum Gangneung Line, pairs beaches with Joseon-era hanok estates and a food scene UNESCO named a Creative City of Gastronomy in 2023.** Start with Ojukheon, birthplace of Shin Saimdang and her son Yulgok, the mother and son on Korea's 50,000- and 5,000-won notes (adults ₩3,000; last entry 17:00), then Seongyojang (adults ₩5,000), Gyeongpo Beach and a bowl of Chodang sundubu.

Source: [Ojukheon Municipal Museum](https://www.gn.go.kr/museum/contents.do?key=891) (Korean), [Korea Heritage Service](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?pageNo=1_1_1_0&ccbaCpno=1123201650000), [Seongyojang](https://www.knsgj.net/tour) (Korean), [Gangneung City](http://www.gn.go.kr/creativecity/html/networks/infor) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=270); checked Oct 30, 2026.

![Graphic: Gangneung at a glance — Ojukheon fees and last entry, Seongyojang, Gyeongpo, Anmok coffee street, Chodang tofu and KTX-Eum](/img/gangneung-steps.png?v=cc79b9a6 "Gangneung at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Why go | East-coast beaches, Joseon-era hanok estates, coffee and tofu |
| UNESCO | Gangneung Danoje Festival (proclaimed 2005, inscribed 2008) · Creative City of Gastronomy (2023) |
| Getting there | KTX-Eum from Seoul Station (adult standard class ₩27,600) or Cheongnyangni (₩26,000); fares from Korail's table as of Sep 1, 2026 |
| Top sights | Ojukheon · Seongyojang · Gyeongpodae and Gyeongpo Beach · Anmok coffee street |
| Eat | Chodang sundubu · potato ongsimi · mulhoe · Jumunjin fish market |

Source: [UNESCO](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/gangneung-danoje-festival-00114), [Gangneung City](http://www.gn.go.kr/creativecity/html/networks/infor) (Korean) and [Korail](https://info.korail.com/info/selectBbsNttView.do?key=911&bbsNo=199&nttNo=25904) (Korean); KTX fares: [Korail fare table](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (as of Sep 1, 2026; Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Ojukheon

![Several tile-roofed hanok buildings behind a low wall and flower beds under a clear sky](/img/photo-gangneung-ojukheon.jpg?v=013cd1b2 "Hanok buildings in the Ojukheon grounds, May 2022. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Ojukheon is the house where Shin Saimdang (1504–1551) and her son Yi I, the Confucian scholar known as Yulgok (1536–1584), were born, the Korea Heritage Service says; Yulgok was born in its Mongryongsil room. It's a Treasure (designated 1963), named for the black bamboo (ojuk) around the house. The Korea Tourism Organization calls it the birthplace of the figures on Korea's banknotes, and the city museum's currency gallery displays the portraits of Yulgok and Saimdang by the artist who drew the 50,000- and 5,000-won note designs.

| | |
|---|---|
| Hours | Entry 09:00–17:00, then you can stay until 18:00 |
| Closed | Open year-round; on Jan 1, Seollal and Chuseok Day the house is open but the indoor exhibition halls close |
| Admission (Ojukheon and the city museum) | Adults ₩3,000 · teenagers ₩2,000 · children ₩1,000 · 65 and over free (bring ID) |
| Discount | 50% off on the last Wednesday of the month ("Culture Day") |
| Parking | Free |

Source: [Ojukheon Municipal Museum — visitor information](https://www.gn.go.kr/museum/contents.do?key=891), [Ojukheon](https://www.gn.go.kr/museum/contents.do?key=897) and [currency gallery](https://www.gn.go.kr/museum/contents.do?key=5614) (Korean); [Korea Heritage Service](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?pageNo=1_1_1_0&ccbaCpno=1123201650000); [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=270); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Arrive by 17:00. Ojukheon's museum says no one is admitted after the entry time, even though the grounds stay open until 18:00.

## Seongyojang

![A wooden hanok building with latticed doors and a name board, beside a gravel yard and trees](/img/photo-gangneung-seongyojang.jpg?v=61883d67 "A hanok building at Seongyojang, May 2022. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Seongyojang is a Joseon-era noble family house that grew over time rather than being built to a single plan; its Yeolhwadang hall dates from 1815. The name means "boat-bridge manor," after the village people once reached by boat. Descendants have lived here for 10 generations over more than 300 years, the heritage service's signboard text says.

| | |
|---|---|
| Hours | 09:00–18:00 in summer · 09:00–17:00 in winter. The site's general footer gives a 17:30 ticket cutoff, which doesn't fit winter closing, so confirm the winter last-entry time before a late visit |
| Admission | Adults ₩5,000 · discounts (teenagers, 65 and over and others) ₩3,000 · children ₩2,000 |
| Guided commentary | On the hour 09:00–16:00 (not 12:00–13:30), 30–40 minutes; the site doesn't say which languages |
| Rules | No pets except guide dogs, no outside food, no drones without permission |

Source: [Seongyojang](https://www.knsgj.net/) and [fees and guiding](https://www.knsgj.net/tour) (Korean) and [Korea Heritage Service](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?pageNo=1_1_2_0&ccbaCpno=1483200050000) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Seongyojang is still a family home, and it posts one-day temporary closures on its notice board (it closed on Oct 20, 2026, for example). Check its [notices](https://www.knsgj.net/) (Korean) before you go.

## Gyeongpodae, Gyeongpo Beach and Anmok coffee street

- **Gyeongpodae Pavilion:** first built in 1326 and later moved and rebuilt, it's a pavilion that poets, calligraphers and painters loved to visit, the Korea Heritage Service says. It became a Treasure in 2019, and the Korea Tourism Organization singles it out for cherry blossom season.
- **Gyeongpo Beach:** about 1.8 km of sand (Gangneung City), which KTO calls one of the most famous beaches on Korea's east coast; Gangneung City lists it as free to visit.
- **Anmok Beach coffee street:** Gangneung's coffee culture began with instant coffee from the vending machines at Anmok, the city says; today there are hundreds of specialty cafés around Gangneung, and the city's coffee festival has run since 2009.

Source: [Korea Heritage Service — Gyeongpodae](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?pageNo=1_1_1_0&ccbaKdcd=12&ccbaAsno=20460000&ccbaCtcd=32&ccbaCpno=1123220460000), [Korea Tourism Organization — course](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=270) and [coffee festival](https://korean.visitkorea.or.kr/detail/fes_detail.do?cotid=e5d334d3-30a3-4c50-8981-03ee9e9489c0) (Korean), [Gangneung City — Gyeongpo Beach](https://www.gn.go.kr/entour/html/entour/sub02/sub02_01_18.jsp) and [coffee](http://www.gn.go.kr/creativecity/html/food/food4) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

![A sandy beach and sea with a few palm trees on the right and small figures of people](/img/photo-gangneung-anmok-beach.jpg?v=93a3c692 "Anmok Beach, April 2022. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Coming for the first sunrise of the year? Gangneung City notes that many visitors come to Gyeongpo Beach for the New Year sunrise and recommends booking a room early. Look for the city's New Year event notice in December.

## What to eat

| Dish | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Chodang sundubu** | Soft tofu traditionally set with East Sea seawater, from Chodang village, named after the pen name of Heo Yeop. About 20 places in Chodang-dong make their own tofu, the city says; look for sundubu gelato and sundubu coffee too |
| **Potato ongsimi** | Dumplings of potato starch cooked in an anchovy, kelp and potato broth, often with buckwheat or knife-cut noodles |
| **Mulhoe** | Cold raw-fish soup; Gangneung's is known for a spicy kick |
| **Jang-kalguksu** | Knife-cut wheat noodles in a spicy anchovy broth seasoned with red chili paste and soybean paste |
| **Jumunjin fish market** | A market dating from 1936 with squid, mackerel, pollack and crab; the city suggests trying snow crab there |

Source: [Gangneung City — UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy](http://www.gn.go.kr/creativecity/html/food/food2) (Korean), [Korea Tourism Organization — Chodang Sundubu Village](https://korean.visitkorea.or.kr/detail/ms_detail.do?cotid=115b36e9-c686-42ff-8f51-714aaf746ba7) (Korean), [Korea Tourism Organization — Jang-kalguksu](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=178864) and [Gangneung City — Jumunjin market](https://www.gn.go.kr/entour/html/entour/sub02/sub02_01_17.jsp); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** "Made with seawater" has a modern twist. A Korea Tourism Organization food guide says Chodang tofu today is made with deep-sea water drawn from more than 200 m down, so ask the restaurant if you're curious.

## Gangneung Danoje Festival

UNESCO describes Gangneung's Danoje as a four-week-long festival around Dano, with a shamanistic ritual on the Daegwallyeong ridge, folk songs and a mask drama. UNESCO proclaimed it a Masterpiece of the Intangible Heritage in 2005 and inscribed it on the Representative List in 2008. Its dates follow the lunar calendar: in 2026 the main festival ran June 15–22. The 2027 dates haven't been announced yet; watch the [festival committee's site](https://www.danojefestival.or.kr/) (Korean).

Source: [UNESCO](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/gangneung-danoje-festival-00114) and [Gangneung Danoje Festival Committee](https://www.danojefestival.or.kr/kor/gdfestival/program_view.html?sd_idx=5) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Getting there and around

| | |
|---|---|
| By train | Take a Gangneung-bound KTX-Eum from Seoul Station or Cheongnyangni. Trains bound for Jeongdongjin and Donghae follow a different branch and don't stop at Gangneung Station, so check the destination when you [book](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) (tickets open at 07:00, two months ahead) |
| KTX fares (adult) | From Seoul Station: standard ₩27,600 · premium class (udeung: fare plus seat surcharge) ₩33,100. From Cheongnyangni: standard ₩26,000 · premium class ₩31,200 |
| Fare condition | Until faster running starts on the Cheongnyangni–Seowonju section, Korail charges this section at a temporary discount. After that, its table shows standard-class fares of ₩30,900 from Seoul and ₩29,200 from Cheongnyangni. Check the fare shown when you book |
| In town | Use [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) for buses or taxis between Ojukheon, Gyeongpo and Anmok |
| Paying | Bring a card and some won: see [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/) |

Source: [Korail — Gangneung Line notice](https://info.korail.com/info/selectBbsNttView.do?key=911&bbsNo=199&nttNo=25904) (Korean), [Korail KTX fare table](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (as of Sep 1, 2026, sheet 19 "Seoul–Cheongnyangni–Gangneung, Donghae"; Korean) and our [KTX booking guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## A one-day plan

> **Our take:** This order keeps the two hanok estates for the morning, when last-entry times aren't a worry, and the sea for the afternoon.

| Time | Where | Why then |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Ojukheon, then Seongyojang | Both close to entry in the late afternoon |
| Lunch | Chodang sundubu | Chodang village is on the way to the coast |
| Afternoon | Gyeongpodae, then Gyeongpo Beach | See the lakeside pavilion, then continue to the beach |
| Late afternoon | Anmok Beach for coffee | Coffee by the sea before your train |

## Before you go

1. Book your KTX-Eum to Gangneung (adult standard class ₩27,600 from Seoul Station, ₩26,000 from Cheongnyangni) and check the fare shown for your train.
2. Reach Ojukheon by 17:00 and check Seongyojang's notices for closures.
3. Visiting on the last Wednesday of the month? Ojukheon is half price.
4. Coming for New Year's sunrise? Book a room early.
5. Install Naver Map for buses and taxis.

Source: [Ojukheon Municipal Museum](https://www.gn.go.kr/museum/contents.do?key=891) (Korean), [Seongyojang](https://www.knsgj.net/) (Korean) and [Gangneung City](https://www.gn.go.kr/entour/html/entour/sub02/sub02_01_01.jsp); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## FAQ

### What is Gangneung known for?

Its beaches, the hanok estates of Ojukheon and Seongyojang, Chodang soft tofu and coffee. UNESCO lists its Danoje Festival and named it a Creative City of Gastronomy in 2023.

### How do I get from Seoul to Gangneung?

Take the KTX-Eum on the Gangneung Line from Seoul Station or Cheongnyangni. Korail's fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026) lists adult standard-class fares of ₩27,600 from Seoul and ₩26,000 from Cheongnyangni, including a temporary discount that ends when faster running starts on the Cheongnyangni–Seowonju section. Check times and the fare shown when you book.

### How much is Ojukheon?

Adults pay ₩3,000, teenagers ₩2,000 and children ₩1,000; people aged 65 and over get in free with ID. Last entry is 17:00.

### What is Chodang sundubu?

Soft tofu from Gangneung's Chodang village, traditionally set with seawater; a Korea Tourism Organization guide describes the village's tofu as now made with deep-sea water, so ask your restaurant.

### When is the Gangneung Danoje Festival?

It follows the lunar calendar, so the dates change each year. In 2026 it ran June 15–22; the 2027 dates haven't been announced yet.

# Tongyeong Travel Guide: Cable Car, Island Ferries and Chungmu Gimbap

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/tongyeong-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-30

## Quick answer

- Tongyeong is a harbor town for islands, seafood and Admiral Yi Sun-sin's naval history. Ride the cable car up Mireuksan (adults ₩17,000 return), see Sebyeonggwan Hall (adults ₩3,000) and take a ferry to Hansan-do.
- Get there by express bus: Seoul Express Bus Terminal to Tongyeong takes about 4 hours 10 minutes (adult fare example ₩42,200, Udeung class). The bus details here were checked on Kobus.
- Bring your passport for island ferries. Foreign passengers show a valid passport (or alien registration card) to board, and you can't board without ID.

**Tongyeong, on Korea's south coast about 4 hours 10 minutes from Seoul by express bus, is the base for the islands of the Hallyeosudo waterway and for Admiral Yi Sun-sin's naval history.** Start with the cable car up Mireuksan (adults ₩17,000 return), Sebyeonggwan Hall, a National Treasure (adults ₩3,000), and Chungmu gimbap by the harbor, then take a ferry to Hansan-do (adult fare example ₩6,300 one way). Bring your passport: island ferries check ID.

Source: [Tongyeong Cable Car](http://cablecar.ttdc.kr/sub02/sub02_01.php) (Korean), [Tongyeong Hansan Daecheop Cultural Foundation](https://tyhansancf.or.kr/facility/facility_01_03.html) (Korean), [Korea Shipping Association](https://island.theksa.co.kr/page/finding_service_fee) (Korean) and [Kobus](https://www.kobus.co.kr/oprninf/alcninqr/oprnAlcnPage.do) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

![Graphic: Tongyeong at a glance — cable car, Sebyeonggwan Hall, the Hansan-do ferry, the express bus from Seoul and what to eat](/img/tongyeong-steps.png?v=d25046b8 "Tongyeong at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Why go | Island views over the Hallyeosudo waterway, Admiral Yi Sun-sin's naval sites and harbor seafood |
| Getting there | Express bus from Seoul, about 4 hours 10 minutes (checked on Kobus) |
| Top sights | Cable car up Mireuksan · Sebyeonggwan Hall (Tongjeyeong) · Hansan-do · Gangguan harbor and Dongpirang |
| Eat | Chungmu gimbap · kkul-ppang (honey bread) · oyster dishes · dajji bars |
| Bring | Your passport, for island ferries |

Source: [Tongyeong City](https://www.utour.go.kr/00413/00414.web), [Kobus](https://www.kobus.co.kr/oprninf/alcninqr/oprnAlcnPage.do) (Korean) and [Korea Shipping Association](https://island.theksa.co.kr/page/bbsCtt?mode=view&bbs_id=notice_booking&bbsctt_seq=16) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

![A rocky island with a lighthouse rising from the sea beyond a green slope, seen from another island](/img/photo-tongyeong-deungdaeseom.jpg?v=919849e1 "Deungdaeseom Island seen from Somaemuldo, May 2019. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

## The cable car and Mireuksan

The cable car runs from the Donam Tourist Complex to just below the peak of Mireuksan, with views over the Hallyeosudo waterway. It's 1,975 m long. From the top, Tongyeong City says, you look out over the waters of the Great Battle of Hansan.

| | Adult | Child (age 4 to elementary school) |
|---|---|---|
| Return | ₩17,000 | ₩13,000 |
| One way | ₩13,500 | ₩11,000 |

- **Regular closing days:** the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of the month (the next day if that's a public holiday).
- **Weather:** the cable car can stop or close in bad weather, so check before you go.
- **Ticket sales** can close 2–3 hours before the end of operation on busy days.
- **November 2026:** closed Nov 2–6 for maintenance; on weekdays it opens at 10:00 and ticket sales end at 16:30. Hours change monthly: check the operator's notices.

Source: [Tongyeong Cable Car — fares and notes](http://cablecar.ttdc.kr/sub02/sub02_01.php), [November 2026 hours](https://cablecar.ttdc.kr/bbs/board.php?bo_table=actTimeInfo&wr_id=21135) and [about the cable car](http://cablecar.ttdc.kr/sub01/sub01_02.php) (Korean); [Tongyeong City](https://www.utour.go.kr/00413/00451/00452.web); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Go in the morning. Ticket sales can close hours before the cable car stops, the operator says, and it has regular closures on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays (the following day when that Wednesday is a public holiday): check the monthly notices.

### Skyline Luge Tongyeong

Skyline Luge Tongyeong has four downhill tracks totaling 3.8 km. A 3-ride ticket is ₩34,000 for an adult. Solo riders must be at least 110 cm tall and 6 years old, subject to staff assessment. Tandem riding has additional age, height and ticket restrictions; meeting the minimum age of 2 and height of 85 cm doesn't by itself establish eligibility. The operator lists an 85–120 cm height band for child doubling tickets and requires a tandem guardian aged 19 or over. Check its detailed height bands and confirm borderline cases with staff before buying a ticket. Show your luge ticket (not just a receipt) at the cable car for ₩2,000 off, within 2 days; with a family ticket the discount covers up to five people, and it can't be combined with other discounts.

Source: [Skyline Luge Tongyeong](https://tongyeong.skylineluge.kr/luge/) (Korean) and [Tongyeong Cable Car — discounts](http://cablecar.ttdc.kr/sub02/sub02_01.php) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Sebyeonggwan Hall and Tongjeyeong

![A large wooden hall with a hipped tile roof and walls, among town buildings](/img/photo-tongyeong-tongjeyeong.jpg?v=c7eb91f7 "Samdo Sugun Tongjeyeong above the town, January 2018. Photo: 95016maphack (CC0), cropped.")

Tongjeyeong was the headquarters of the Joseon navy's commander of the three southern provinces, in use until 1895. Its main hall, **Sebyeonggwan**, was first built in 1605 and rebuilt on a larger scale in 1646; it's a National Treasure (designated 2002). Tongyeong City calls it one of the largest Joseon-era buildings by floor area, open-sided, with no walls or windows between its 50 columns, and says the name means "washing weapons in the stream of the Milky Way."

| | |
|---|---|
| Hours | The foundation that runs it lists 09:00–18:00 with last tickets at 17:30, but the city lists a 17:00 closing from November to February. Confirm the current cutoff, and don't plan a 17:30 arrival in winter |
| Admission | Adults ₩3,000 · teenagers ₩2,000 · children ₩1,000 |
| Free day | The last Wednesday of the month ("Culture Day") |
| Discount | 20% off with a Tongyeong cable car ticket |
| Getting there | Get off at the Tongyeong Depart (통영데파트) bus stop, about a minute's walk |
| Evening visits | Check the current opening and last-entry times before going inside. Don't use sunset as a substitute for the ticket cutoff or closing time. After closing, view the illuminated buildings from outside |

Source: [Tongyeong Hansan Daecheop Cultural Foundation](https://tyhansancf.or.kr/facility/facility_01_03.html) (Korean), [Korea Heritage Service](https://www.heritage.go.kr/heri/cul/culSelectDetail.do?ccbaKdcd=11&ccbaAsno=03050000&ccbaCtcd=38) (Korean), [Tongyeong City — Sebyeonggwan](https://www.utour.go.kr/00056/00350/00351.web?amode=view&idx=1634) and [Tongjeyeong](https://www.utour.go.kr/00056/00350/00351.web?amode=view&idx=1698) (Korean) and [fees](https://www.utour.go.kr/00152/00154/00162.web) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Hansan-do: Admiral Yi's island

Hansan-do is where Admiral Yi Sun-sin set up his naval command during the Japanese invasions: in August 1593 he built the Unjudang there. It was destroyed in 1597, and **Jeseungdang**, the hall you visit today, was rebuilt on its site in 1740. Tongyeong City's fee list shows Jeseungdang as free.

| Ferry from Tongyeong to Hansan-do (Jeseungdang) | |
|---|---|
| Adult fare example | ₩6,300 one way |
| Sailings | Vary by day: on the dates we checked, the first left at 07:00 and the last at 16:30, with 9 sailings on a Saturday and 6 on a Monday |
| Booking | Korea Shipping Association's island ferry site (Korean); some sailings sell out online, so book ahead or call the operator |
| ID | Required to board |

Source: [Tongyeong City — Hansando](https://www.utour.go.kr/00456/00460/00461.web) and [Jeseungdang](https://www.utour.go.kr/00456/00460/00462.web), [fees](https://www.utour.go.kr/00152/00154/00162.web) (Korean) and [Korea Shipping Association — timetable and fares](https://island.theksa.co.kr/page/finding_service_fee) (Korean, searched for Oct 31 and Nov 2, 2026); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Island ferries check ID when you board, and you can't board without it, even with a mobile or online ticket. Foreign passengers can use a valid passport or an alien registration card, the Korea Shipping Association says.

## Gangguan harbor, Dongpirang and the markets

![Calm water with a small wooded islet and a shipyard with cranes along the shore, mountains behind under a cloudy sky](/img/photo-tongyeong-port.jpg?v=daa1eedd "Tongyeong Port, August 2023. Photo: Dittwjfsdgkvkdjg (CC BY-SA 3.0), cropped.")

- **Gangguan:** the old harbor in the middle of town. Nearby are exhibits of Joseon-era warships, including the Geobukseon (turtle ship) and the panokseon, Tongyeong City says.
- **Dongpirang:** a hillside village above Gangguan where the murals along its winding lanes are renewed through painting contests. At the top, the Dongporu pavilion looks over the harbor.
- **Jungang Market:** across from Gangguan, a seafood market selling fish caught off Tongyeong, the city says. **Seoho Market** is the town's other traditional market.

Source: [Tongyeong City — Gangguan](https://www.utour.go.kr/00413/00414.web), [markets](https://www.utour.go.kr/00516/00518.web) and [Dongpirang](https://www.utour.go.kr/00056/00058/00072.web?amode=view&idx=1639) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Dongpirang is a real neighborhood. The city says its shops and cafés close in the evening and asks visitors to keep quiet at night, so go in daylight.

## What to eat

| Dish | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Chungmu gimbap** | Plain rice rolls with no filling, served with radish kimchi, a spicy octopus dish and seasoned cuttlefish on the side. Look around Gangguan, the ferry terminal and the excursion boat terminal |
| **Kkul-ppang (honey bread)** | Red bean filling wrapped in dough, fried, then coated in syrup and sesame |
| **Oysters** | Oyster rice, stew, grilled, steamed or raw; the city's oyster festival is usually held around November |
| **Dajji** | Bars where you order drinks and the dishes come with them; there's no set menu, and dishes depend on the day's fresh ingredients |

Source: [Tongyeong City — food](https://www.utour.go.kr/00516/00517.web) and [markets](https://www.utour.go.kr/00516/00518.web), [Hallyeosudo oyster festival](https://www.utour.go.kr/00056/00060/00087.web?amode=view&idx=2223) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

Spring visitor? The Tongyeong International Music Festival, dedicated to the Tongyeong-born composer Yun Isang, is held from late March to early April each year; the city advises booking a room early for festival dates. Dates are announced on [timf.org](https://www.timf.org/kr/sub/business/festival.asp).

## A two-day plan

> **Our take:** The bus ride is long, so stay a night. This order keeps the cable car for a morning and reserves an afternoon for Hansan-do; check the last return boat and your bus back before you go.

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bus from Seoul | Sebyeonggwan Hall (before last ticket), Gangguan and Dongpirang | Jungang Market, Chungmu gimbap |
| 2 | Cable car up Mireuksan | Ferry to Hansan-do and Jeseungdang | Bus back to Seoul |

## Before you go

1. Book your express bus from Seoul and plan to stay a night.
2. Pack your passport for island ferries.
3. Check the cable car's monthly notices: regular closures fall on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays (the next day when that Wednesday is a public holiday).
4. Check Hansan-do sailings on the Korea Shipping Association site the day before.
5. Visit Sebyeonggwan Hall well before closing: the official winter hours differ (17:00 or 18:00), so confirm the cutoff.

Source: [Tongyeong Cable Car](http://cablecar.ttdc.kr/sub02/sub02_01.php) (Korean), [Korea Shipping Association](https://island.theksa.co.kr/page/bbsCtt?mode=view&bbs_id=notice_booking&bbsctt_seq=16) (Korean) and [Tongyeong Hansan Daecheop Cultural Foundation](https://tyhansancf.or.kr/facility/facility_01_03.html) (Korean); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## FAQ

### How do I get from Seoul to Tongyeong?

By express bus from Seoul Express Bus Terminal, about 4 hours 10 minutes. An adult Udeung-class fare example is ₩42,200; premium buses cost more.

### Is there a train to Tongyeong?

For this trip, plan on the express bus from Seoul: the city's transport guide lists bus routes, and the bus times and fares here were checked on Kobus.

### How much is the Tongyeong cable car?

Adults pay ₩17,000 return or ₩13,500 one way. It has regular closures on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays (the next day if that Wednesday is a public holiday) and can stop in bad weather.

### Do I need a passport for the ferry to Hansan-do?

You need an accepted ID: a valid passport is the simplest option for short-term visitors, and an alien registration card also works. Island ferries check ID when you board.

### Is Tongyeong worth visiting?

In our view, yes, for island views, Admiral Yi's naval history and harbor food like Chungmu gimbap. Stay at least one night: the bus from Seoul takes about 4 hours.

# Bringing Medicine into Korea: Limits, Prescriptions and the Narcotics Permit

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/bringing-medicine-into-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-30

## Quick answer

- Ordinary medicine for your own use: up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply, per the Korea Customs Service. Carry proof it's yours — a prescription, a doctor's letter or the pharmacy label — and keep it in its original packaging.
- Medicines with narcotic or psychotropic ingredients (for example zolpidem, alprazolam, diazepam or Ritalin) need a permit from Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) before you travel, whatever your nationality. You apply online; allow at least 10 working days.
- Not sure? Check by active ingredient, not brand name, and ask MFDS or Korea Customs (call 125) before you fly. Undeclared or unapproved medicines can be held at the airport.

**You can bring ordinary medicine into Korea for your own use — up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply, according to the Korea Customs Service — but medicines with narcotic or psychotropic ingredients need a permit from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) before you arrive, whatever your nationality.** Carry proof the medicine is yours: a prescription, a doctor's letter or the pharmacy label.

Source: [Korea Customs Service guide via the Korean Embassy in Denmark](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1) (Aug 2023) and [MFDS](https://www.mfds.go.kr/brd/m_74/view.do?seq=43906); checked Oct 28, 2026.

This guide covers medicine only. For the rest of your packing and the arrival forms, see the [Korea first-timer checklist](/korea-first-time-checklist/). It isn't medical or legal advice — the rules go by active ingredient, so check your own medicines with the agencies below.

![Graphic: Bringing medicine into Korea at a glance — up to 6 bottles or 3 months, carry proof, narcotic or psychotropic drugs need an MFDS permit, duty may apply over US$800, ask Customs 125](/img/medicine-steps.png?v=a555e812 "Bringing medicine into Korea at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| Your medicine | What the rules say | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary medicine for yourself | Up to **6 bottles or a 3-month supply** | Carry a prescription, doctor's letter or pharmacy label; keep the original packaging |
| Health supplements ("health functional foods") | Up to **6 bottles** | Keep them in original containers |
| Narcotic or psychotropic medicine (e.g. zolpidem, alprazolam, diazepam, lorazepam, Ritalin) | Not allowed **without an MFDS permit** | Apply online to MFDS before you travel |
| Viagra or Cialis | Treated as medicines with misuse concerns | Customs clears only the quantity on a prescription from a Korean doctor |
| More than the limits — or restricted ingredients, unclear labels | Needs a separate import-requirement check | Ask Korea Customs before you fly |

Source: [Korea Customs Service guide](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1) (Aug 2023); checked Oct 28, 2026.

## 1. Ordinary medicine: 6 bottles or 3 months

The Korea Customs Service guide says travelers can, in principle, bring medicine **for personal use, up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply**. The Korean Embassy notice that shares the guide adds what to carry:

- **Proof it's yours** — a prescription, a medical certificate or the pharmacy label on the package.
- **Proof you bought it lawfully** — you may be asked for a receipt.
- **The original packaging** — recommended, so officers can see what it is.

Two things to watch:

- **Value:** duty can be charged if your goods total more than **US$800**, even within the 6-bottle or 3-month limit. US$800 is also the general duty-free allowance listed by Incheon Airport.
- **The limit isn't the whole story.** Korea Customs says medicine within the duty-free clearance scope is exempt from the separate import-requirement check, but medicine beyond that scope needs the check (a doctor's note listing the items can help for your own treatment). Some products need the check **even within the limit**: ones containing CITES-listed ingredients, products MFDS has banned or flagged as harmful, and packages without a clear ingredient label. If in doubt, ask Customs about your specific medicine.

Source: [Korea Customs Service guide and embassy notice](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1), [Incheon Customs — medicines and health supplements](https://customs.go.kr/incheon/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=5480&mi=10560) (Korean) and [Incheon Airport — customs](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1445/subview.do); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## 2. Narcotic and psychotropic medicine: get the MFDS permit first

Since October 23, 2009, anyone entering Korea with medicine that contains a **narcotic or psychotropic substance** for their own treatment must get MFDS approval first — **Korean or foreign, it doesn't matter**.

The Customs guide names medicines that can't be brought in without following the legal procedure, including **zolpidem, alprazolam, diazepam, lorazepam and Ritalin**. "Narcotics, psychotropic drugs and related products" are also on Incheon Airport's list of prohibited items.

Source: [MFDS notice](https://www.mfds.go.kr/brd/m_74/view.do?seq=43906), [Korea Customs Service guide](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1) and [Incheon Airport](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1445/subview.do); checked Oct 28, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Don't bring ordinary cannabis products such as CBD oils, vape cartridges or cannabis-infused drinks. [Incheon Customs](https://customs.go.kr/incheon/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=5480&mi=10560) (Korean) warns that unauthorized import can lead to criminal penalties. Cannabis-based medicines for self-treatment have a separate prior-approval route under [Korean law](https://www.law.go.kr/LSW/lsSideInfoP.do?lsiSeq=290391&joNo=0003&joBrNo=00&docCls=jo&urlMode=lsScJoRltInfoR) (Korean): confirm your exact medicine and get the required MFDS approval before you travel. A foreign prescription alone is not approval.

**How to apply (online since December 27, 2024):**

1. Go to **Drug Safety Korea** ([nedrug.mfds.go.kr/eng/index](https://nedrug.mfds.go.kr/eng/index)) and choose **"Permit To Bring In Narcotics For Self-treatment."**
2. **Verify your email** and set a password — the site uses email login.
3. Fill in your **name, passport number, nationality, dates in Korea and flight number**, then the **medicine, its active ingredient and your dose**.
4. **Attach your documents:** a full-size copy of your passport and your flight reservation (plus proof of a long stay, if that applies). For the medical part, follow the form's options: normally a medical certificate or doctor's letter and a valid prescription. If your country's government issues an official export/import certificate for narcotic or psychotropic medicine, the manual says you can upload that instead of the medical letter and prescription.
5. **Submit** and track the result in the same system.

Source: [MFDS — online application user manual](https://www.mfds.go.kr/brd/m_74/view.do?seq=43906) (English attachment); checked Oct 28, 2026.

**Allow at least 10 working days.** A Korean consulate's guide to the online permit says processing takes 10 working days, so you should apply at least 10 days before you arrive — and an application with missing documents, or one filed too late, may be returned. Apply earlier in case MFDS asks for more documents.

Source: [Consulate General of Korea in Los Angeles — online permit guide](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/us-honolulu-ko/brd/m_27261/view.do?seq=1344065) (Korean, Jun 2025); checked Oct 29, 2026.

Questions go to the MFDS Narcotics Policy Division: **+82-43-719-2813** or **narcotics@korea.kr**. The permit comes from MFDS, not from Korean embassies.

## 3. Viagra, Cialis and "health" products

The Customs guide lists **Viagra and Cialis** as medicines with a high risk of misuse. For these, customs clears **only the quantity on a Korean doctor's prescription**. It also warns that fake sexual enhancers are strictly controlled.

Traditional remedies need care too: products such as **bear bile powder** that aren't clearly labeled are refused entry under the Customs Act.

Source: [Korea Customs Service guide](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1); checked Oct 28, 2026.

## 4. If customs holds your medicine

- Held medicine is released only with confirming documents — the guide gives **a prescription from a Korean doctor** as the example.
- You can ask to have held items returned (sent back abroad), following customs' return procedure.
- The guide warns that held items can be **discarded after one month**. Ask the customs office holding your medicine which deadline applies to you.

Source: [Korea Customs Service guide](https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1); checked Oct 28, 2026.

## 5. Declaring at the airport

If you have something to declare — for example medicine over the limits, or goods over US$800 — fill in the customs declaration form and use the **"Goods to Declare"** lane. Korea Customs says that if undeclared goods over the duty-free allowance are found, you pay an **additional tax of 40% of the tax due**. It rises to **60%** if, counting back two years from your entry date, you have **already been charged this surcharge at least twice** — in effect, from the third time. Medicine-related violations can carry separate penalties, so ask Korea Customs about your case.

Source: [Korea Customs Service — traveller declarations](https://www2.customs.go.kr/kcs/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=829&mi=2837) (Korean), the [Enforcement Decree of the Customs Act, Article 247(4)](https://www.law.go.kr/LSW/lsSideInfoP.do?docCls=jo&joBrNo=00&joNo=0247&lsiSeq=283621&urlMode=lsScJoRltInfoR) (Korean) and [Incheon Airport — customs](https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1445/subview.do); checked Oct 30, 2026.

## Before you fly

1. **List your medicines by active ingredient**, not brand name.
2. Anything narcotic or psychotropic? **Apply for the MFDS permit** online — at least 10 working days before you arrive.
3. Keep **6 bottles or 3 months' supply or less**, in the **original packaging**.
4. Pack the **prescription or doctor's letter** in your carry-on, with the medicine.
5. Unsure? Ask **Korea Customs** ([English Q&A](https://www.customs.go.kr/english/ad/engcnsl/selectEngCnslList.do?mi=8049), or call **125** in Korea, weekdays 09:00–18:00).

If you need a doctor or pharmacy while you're in Korea, see [emergency help in Korea](/emergency-help-korea/).

## FAQ

### How much medicine can I bring into Korea?

For ordinary medicine for your own use, up to 6 bottles or a 3-month supply, according to the Korea Customs Service. Duty can apply if your goods total more than US$800.

### Do I need a prescription to bring medicine into Korea?

You need to show the medicine is for your own use — a prescription, medical certificate or pharmacy label works. Narcotic or psychotropic medicine also needs an MFDS permit before you travel.

### Can I bring zolpidem (Ambien) or Xanax to Korea?

Zolpidem and alprazolam (the active ingredient in Xanax) are on the Customs guide's list of psychotropic drugs. You need an MFDS permit, applied for online before you travel.

### Can I bring ADHD medication to Korea?

Ritalin is on the Customs guide's psychotropic list, so it needs an MFDS permit. For other ADHD medicines, check the active ingredient with MFDS before you fly.

### Who do I ask if I'm not sure?

For narcotic or psychotropic medicine, the MFDS Narcotics Policy Division (+82-43-719-2813, narcotics@korea.kr). For everything else, Korea Customs (call 125 in Korea, or the English Q&A online).

## Sources

- Korea Customs Service, Incheon — Traveler customs clearance (Korean): https://customs.go.kr/incheon/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=5480&mi=10560
- Korea Customs Service — Customs clearance of medications, health functional foods and psychotropic drugs (guide shared by the Korean Embassy in Denmark, Aug 2023): https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/dk-en/brd/m_7038/view.do?seq=761250&page=1
- Ministry of Food and Drug Safety — Permit to bring in narcotics for self-treatment (online since Dec 27, 2024): https://www.mfds.go.kr/brd/m_74/view.do?seq=43906
- Ministry of Food and Drug Safety — Drug Safety Korea, English site (permit application): https://nedrug.mfds.go.kr/eng/index
- Incheon International Airport — Customs: duty-free allowance and prohibited items: https://www.airport.kr/ap_en/1445/subview.do
- Korea Customs Service — Traveller declarations and penalties (Korean): https://www2.customs.go.kr/kcs/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=829&mi=2837
- Korean Law Information Center — Enforcement Decree of the Customs Act, Article 247 (Korean): https://www.law.go.kr/LSW/lsSideInfoP.do?docCls=jo&joBrNo=00&joNo=0247&lsiSeq=283621&urlMode=lsScJoRltInfoR
- Korea Customs Service — English Q&A: https://www.customs.go.kr/english/ad/engcnsl/selectEngCnslList.do?mi=8049
- Incheon Customs — Medicines and health supplements for personal use (Korean): https://customs.go.kr/incheon/cm/cntnts/cntntsView.do?cntntsId=5480&mi=10560
- Consulate General of Korea in Los Angeles — Online permit for narcotic medicines (Korean, Jun 2025): https://overseas.mofa.go.kr/us-honolulu-ko/brd/m_27261/view.do?seq=1344065

# Korean Convenience Stores: Medicine, Alcohol Age, Tax Refunds and More

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/korea-convenience-store-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-29

## Quick answer

- Medicine: registered 24-hour stores can sell 13 government-approved over-the-counter medicines, such as Tylenol and digestive tablets — one pack of each per purchase, and not to children under 12 or to elementary school pupils of any age.
- Alcohol and tobacco: you must not be a 'youth' under Korean law — in 2026 that means born in 2007 or earlier. Staff must check age, so carry your passport.
- Instant tax refund at CU: at participating CU stores, show your passport for up to 7% off purchases of ₩15,000–₩999,999 (not alcohol, tobacco or hot food).

**Korean convenience stores — chains such as GS25, CU, 7-Eleven and emart24 — do far more than sell snacks: registered 24-hour stores can sell 13 government-approved medicines, you can buy and top up a T-money card, and participating CU stores give instant tax refunds with your passport.** To buy alcohol or tobacco you must not count as a "youth" under Korean law; in 2026 that means you were born in 2007 or earlier.

Source: [Ministry of Health and Welfare](https://www.mohw.go.kr/menu.es?mid=a10702040200), [Youth Protection Act](https://www.law.go.kr/lsInfoP.do?lsiSeq=285397) and [CU — tax refund](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/tax_info.do?category=service&depth3=19) (all Korean), and the [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140663); checked Oct 29, 2026.

![Graphic: Korean convenience stores at a glance — 13 approved medicines, alcohol for those born in 2007 or earlier, instant tax refund at CU, T-money top-up with cash](/img/cstore-steps.png?v=17cb1867 "Korean convenience stores at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| You want to… | What to know |
|---|---|
| Buy painkillers or cold medicine at night | Registered 24-hour stores sell 13 approved medicines — one pack of each per purchase |
| Buy beer, soju or cigarettes | Born in 2007 or earlier (2026 rule). Carry your passport |
| Get a tax refund on the spot | Participating CU stores: ₩15,000–₩999,999 per payment, show your passport |
| Get or top up a T-money card | Any major chain; top up with Korean won cash |
| Withdraw cash | Many stores have an ATM — CU lists withdrawals among its ATM services |
| Send a parcel or charge your phone | CU takes parcels 24/7 and rents power banks at some stores |

Source: as listed in each section below; checked Oct 29, 2026.

The Korea Tourism Organization says many convenience stores, like many ATMs, are open 24/7 all year — but not every store is.

## Medicine: 13 approved over-the-counter products

Korea lets some shops that aren't pharmacies sell a short list of "household safety medicines." The rules are in the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act and its enforcement rule:

- **Only registered stores open 24 hours a day, every day of the year** can sell them, and the registration certificate must be displayed in the store.
- **One pack of each product per purchase.**
- **Not to children under 12** — or to elementary school pupils, whatever their age.

The Ministry of Health and Welfare's list has **13 products**:

| Type | Products (our English rendering) | Korean name on the list |
|---|---|---|
| Fever and pain relief | Tylenol 500 mg, Tylenol 160 mg, Children's Tylenol 80 mg, Children's Tylenol suspension, Children's Brufen syrup | 타이레놀정 500mg, 타이레놀정 160mg, 어린이용 타이레놀정 80mg, 어린이타이레놀현탁액, 어린이부루펜시럽 |
| Indigestion | Bearse, Dr. Bearse, Festal Gold, Festal Plus | 베아제정, 닥터베아제정, 훼스탈골드정, 훼스탈플러스정 |
| Colds | Pancol-A oral solution, Panpyrin-T | 판콜에이내복액, 판피린티정 |
| Pain patches | Jeil Cool Pap, Shinshin Pas Arex | 제일쿨파프, 신신파스아렉스 |

The English names are only to help you recognize the Korean products; similar-looking products in other strengths or forms aren't necessarily on the list.

Source: [Ministry of Health and Welfare](https://www.mohw.go.kr/menu.es?mid=a10702040200), last updated Mar 31, 2026; [Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, Article 44-2](https://www.law.go.kr/lsInfoP.do?lsiSeq=285341) and [Enforcement Rule, Article 28](https://www.law.go.kr/lsInfoP.do?lsiSeq=287367) (all Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

Not every store stocks every product. For anything else — or if you're unsure what to take — go to a pharmacy. If it's urgent, see our [emergency help guide](/emergency-help-korea/).

## Alcohol and tobacco: the age rule

Under the Youth Protection Act, a "youth" is anyone **under 19**, except that you stop counting as a youth on **January 1 of the year you turn 19**. Nobody may sell alcohol or tobacco to a youth, and the seller **must check the buyer's age and identity**.

In practice, in 2026 that means **people born in 2007 or earlier** can buy. Carry your passport — staff are required to check.

Source: [Youth Protection Act, Articles 2 and 28](https://www.law.go.kr/lsInfoP.do?lsiSeq=285397) (Korean), as in force from Oct 8, 2026; checked Oct 29, 2026.

## Instant tax refund at CU

CU offers instant tax refunds at **participating stores** — up to **7% off** the price.

| | |
|---|---|
| Who | Foreign tourists (staying in Korea less than 6 months) and overseas Koreans who meet CU's conditions |
| Amount | ₩15,000 to ₩999,999 per payment |
| Not included | Alcohol, tobacco, tax-free goods (such as plain milk, fruit and vegetables), food cooked in store, and services |
| How | Ask for a tax refund at the counter, show your passport (physical or mobile), and pay the reduced price |
| Also required | The general tourist-refund rules: goods must be new (unopened and unused), and you must leave Korea within three months of buying them |

Source: [CU — tax refund](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/tax_info.do?category=service&depth3=19) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

The Korea Tourism Organization adds that your instant-refund purchases over the whole trip can't go over ₩5,000,000, and that refunds are for new, unopened and unused goods taken out of Korea within three months of purchase — so snacks you eat in Korea aren't what the scheme is for. The general rules are in our [Korea tax refund guide](/korea-tax-refund-guide/).

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — tax refunds](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140736); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## T-money: buy, top up, small refunds

The Korea Tourism Organization says you can buy and load T-money cards at convenience stores nationwide, including GS25, CU and 7-Eleven, and that smaller balances can be refunded there.

- **Top up with cash.** T-money says cash is the most reliable way at convenience stores, and you shouldn't assume a foreign credit card can top up a standard physical card.
- **Under 18?** The Korea Tourism Organization says young travelers register their date of birth at a convenience store to get the youth or child fare.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — transportation cards](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140663) and [T-money](https://blog.tmoney.co.kr/en/tmoney-guide/tmoney-convenience-store-guide/); checked Oct 29, 2026.

Fares, refund limits and where else to buy one: see our [T-money card guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## ATMs, parcels and power banks (CU)

These are CU's own services; other chains may offer similar ones, but we haven't checked them.

- **ATM:** CU says the cash machines in its stores offer cash withdrawals, transfers and credit card cash advances. It doesn't say whether foreign cards work, and not every store has one — CU's store finder shows which do. For cash and cards in general, see our [payment guide](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).
- **Parcels:** CU accepts parcels 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with fares from ₩3,400 depending on weight and destination.
- **Power banks:** at some CU stores you can rent a power bank and return it at any rental station.

Source: CU — [ATM](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/ticket_info.do?category=service&depth3=2), [parcels](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/parcel_info.do?category=service&depth3=4) and [power banks](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/frugal_info.do?category=service&depth3=9) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## Small things worth knowing

- **Bags:** Korea restricts disposable bags in shops. The environment ministry said in 2023 that many stores, convenience stores included, use alternatives such as reusable bags, biodegradable bags and the pay-per-use rubbish bags. A small foldable bag of your own helps.
- **At the airport:** the Korea Tourism Organization says the clear plastic bags needed for liquids at security are sold at convenience stores, drug stores and bookstores inside the airport.
- **Food:** convenience stores sell gimbap and other snacks — see our [Korean street food guide](/korean-street-food/).
- **SIM cards:** some convenience stores sell them — see our [eSIM and SIM card guide](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/).

> **Local tip:** K-pop fans, look for a kiosk. Some CU stores have one where you can buy artists' albums and merchandise and print a photocard when you buy an album that comes with one; [CU](https://cu.bgfretail.com/service/kiosk_kpop.do?category=service&depth3=21) (Korean) says it's available at stores with a kiosk installed.

Source: [Korea Policy Briefing, Nov 9, 2023](https://www.korea.kr/briefing/policyBriefingView.do?newsId=156598864) (Korean) and [Korea Tourism Organization — airport security](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/infoHtmlView.do?vcontsId=140628); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## FAQ

### Can you buy medicine at Korean convenience stores?

Yes, at registered 24-hour stores: 13 approved products, including Tylenol, children's fever medicine, digestive tablets, two cold medicines and pain patches. You can buy one pack of each per purchase, and they can't be sold to children under 12 or to elementary school pupils of any age.

### What is the drinking age in Korea?

You can buy alcohol from January 1 of the year you turn 19. In 2026 that means people born in 2007 or earlier. Sellers must check age and identity, so carry your passport.

### Can I get a tax refund at a convenience store?

At participating CU stores, yes: show your passport for an instant refund of up to 7% on payments of ₩15,000–₩999,999. Alcohol, tobacco, tax-free goods and food cooked in store don't count, and the goods must be new, unopened and unused and leave Korea with you within three months.

### Can I top up T-money with a credit card at a convenience store?

Plan on cash. T-money says cash is the most reliable way at convenience stores and that a foreign credit card may not work for topping up a standard card.

### Are Korean convenience stores open 24 hours?

Many are, according to the Korea Tourism Organization, but not all. Medicines are sold only at registered stores that are open 24 hours, every day.

# Lotte World and Seoul Sky: Tickets, Hours and Tips for One Day in Jamsil

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/lotte-world-seoul-sky-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-29

## Quick answer

- Lotte World Adventure: park-only 1-day ticket ₩64,000 for adults (19+), ₩56,000 for ages 13–18, ₩49,000 for ages 3–12. After 4 p.m. it's ₩52,000 for adults. Mostly indoors.
- Seoul Sky (Lotte World Tower): ₩33,000 for ages 13+ and ₩29,000 for ages 3–12. The observatory is about 500 m up; the Sky Bridge tour costs extra, has height, weight and age limits, and is best booked online in advance.
- Same station: both are at Jamsil Station (Lines 2 and 8). Both close ticket sales and entry one hour before closing — and hours change by day.

**A park-only day ticket for Lotte World Adventure costs ₩64,000 for adults (19 and over), and Seoul Sky, the observatory in Lotte World Tower next door, costs ₩33,000 for anyone 13 and over.** Both are at Jamsil Station in southeast Seoul, so you can do the theme park and the view in one day for ₩97,000 per adult. Hours change by day, and both stop selling tickets one hour before closing.

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — tickets](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/price/price) and [Seoul Sky — tickets](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/price/info/ticket) (both Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

**Watch the age bands:** an "adult" is 19 and over at Lotte World Adventure but 13 and over at Seoul Sky. A 15-year-old pays the youth price at the park and the adult price at the tower.

![Graphic: Lotte World and Seoul Sky at a glance — park ticket from ₩64,000, Seoul Sky ₩33,000, Jamsil Station Lines 2 and 8, last entry one hour before closing](/img/lotte-steps.png?v=8a07d5a9 "Lotte World and Seoul Sky at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | Lotte World Adventure | Seoul Sky |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Theme park, mostly indoors under a glass dome, plus Magic Island outdoors on Seokchon Lake | Observatory at the top of Lotte World Tower (123 floors, 555 m) |
| Adult ticket | ₩64,000 park-only, 1 day (19+) | ₩33,000 (13+) |
| Hours (days we checked) | 10:00–21:00 or 10:00–22:00 | 10:30–22:00, or 10:30–23:00 on Fri and Sat |
| Last entry | 1 hour before closing | 1 hour before closing |
| Subway | Jamsil Station, Lines 2 and 8, Exit 4 | Jamsil Station, Line 2 Exits 1–2 or Line 8 Exits 10–11 |

Source: [Lotte World Adventure](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/usage-guide/service/closed) and [Seoul Sky](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/guide/hours) opening-hours calendars (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## Lotte World Adventure tickets

There are two kinds of ticket. The **park ticket** covers the park and its rides (not paid extras such as game arcades). The **combined ticket** adds the Lotte World Folk Museum (last museum entry 18:00).

| Ticket | Adult (19+) | Youth (13–18) | Child (36 months–12) | Baby (12 to under 36 months) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Park, 1 day | ₩64,000 | ₩56,000 | ₩49,000 | ₩17,000 |
| Park, After 4 | ₩52,000 | ₩45,000 | ₩38,000 | ₩17,000 |
| Combined (park + Folk Museum), 1 day | ₩67,000 | ₩58,000 | ₩50,000 | ₩17,000 |
| Combined, After 4 | ₩55,000 | ₩47,000 | ₩39,000 | ₩17,000 |

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — tickets](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/price/price) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

- **After 4** tickets let you in from 4 p.m. On a day the park closes at 21:00 or 22:00, that's five or six hours.
- **Babies:** under 12 months get in free, with the infant rides. From 12 months to under 36 months, park entry is free (except for group visitors), but the baby ticket is needed for the designated infant rides. From 36 months, the child fare applies. Bring an ID or document that shows the child's age.
- **65 and over** pay the regular child price, the park says, with no other discounts on top.
- **Disability:** 50% off the park or combined ticket for the visitor and one companion, with official proof.
- **Combined tickets need a physical ticket.** The park says a screenshot on your phone isn't accepted — if you buy online, check with the seller how to collect it.

## Magic Pass: skip the queues (extra cost)

The Magic Pass gets you into a dedicated line for five rides (you may still wait a little, some rides can only be used once, and some attractions are excluded). It's **sold only in the Lotte World app**, in limited numbers each day, and it **doesn't include admission** — you still need a park or combined ticket.

| Magic Pass (5 rides) | Price |
|---|---|
| Light | ₩54,000 |
| Standard A | ₩65,000 |
| Standard B | ₩65,000 |
| Premium | ₩80,000 |

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — Magic Pass](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/price/price/magicpass) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

- **When to buy:** all types go on sale in the app from **08:30 on the day**. Only Premium can be booked ahead, from midnight two days before your visit until 23:59 the day before.
- **Limits:** up to 4 per person, one pass per rider. Each type covers a different set of rides, so check the list before you pay.
- **Refunds:** an unused same-day pass can be cancelled for a full refund within 2 hours of purchase. Once you've used it on a ride, or after 2 hours, there's no refund. Premium passes booked ahead can be cancelled until 23:30 the day before.

## Hours, weather and ride closures

Lotte World Adventure's opening hours change by date. On the days we checked it opened at 10:00 and closed at 21:00 (Thu Oct 29, 2026) or 22:00 (Fri Oct 30 and Sat Oct 31). **Ticket sales and entry end one hour before closing**, and the opening time can shift with crowds at the gate.

- **Magic Island is outdoors.** Some rides there may stop when it's 0°C or colder, 30°C or hotter, windy, or raining — the park lists 0.2 mm of rain as one trigger.
- **Rides close for maintenance on set days.** The park's calendar lists which rides are closed each day — check it if there's one you came for.

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — opening hours and ride closures](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/usage-guide/service/closed) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

> **Local tip:** On a cold or rainy day, plan around the indoor Adventure area under the dome, and check Magic Island ride status once you're inside.

## Park rules worth knowing

- **No alcohol, no pets** (guide and assistance dogs are allowed), **no drones**, and no picnic mats — a one-person cushion or folding chair is fine.
- **The whole park is non-smoking** except the designated smoking room.
- **No rides after drinking.**

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — park rules](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/usage-guide/service/park) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

## Seoul Sky tickets

Seoul Sky sits at the top of **Lotte World Tower — 123 floors and 555 m tall**. The observatory is about 500 m up. It also has an outdoor terrace on the 120th floor (486 m) and a glass-floored Sky Deck (478 m).

| Ticket | Adult (13+) | Child (36 months–12) |
|---|---|---|
| Regular | ₩33,000 | ₩29,000 |
| Seoul Sky + Lotte World Aquarium | ₩62,000 | ₩56,000 (also ages 65+) |
| Fast Pass (enter without a reservation) | ₩62,000, all ages | |

Source: [Seoul Sky — tickets](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/price/info/ticket) and [about Seoul Sky](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/intro) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

- **Where to buy:** online, on mobile, or at the ticket office.
- **Under 36 months** get in free with a guardian — bring proof of age.
- **Timed tickets:** if your ticket has an entry time, be at the observatory by that time.
- **No copies or screenshots** of tickets are accepted.
- The aquarium package must be used **on the same day** for both places.
- **Disability:** 30% off for the visitor and one companion, with official proof.

### Seoul Sky hours

Seoul Sky opened at **10:30** on the days we checked, closing at **22:00** (Thu Oct 29 and Mon Nov 2, 2026) or **23:00** (Fri Oct 30 and Sat Oct 31). **Ticket sales and entry end one hour before closing.** The calendar on the official site shows each day's hours.

Source: [Seoul Sky — opening hours](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/guide/hours) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026.

### The Sky Bridge (limits apply; booking ahead recommended)

The Sky Bridge is a guided walk on a bridge at the very top, 541 m up. It's a separate ticket:

| Where you buy | Price | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| B1 ticket office | ₩130,000 | Observatory admission, the tour and 2 photos |
| 117F Sky Station (already inside) | ₩106,000 | The tour and 2 photos |

Source: [Seoul Sky — Sky Bridge prices](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/price/info/sky-bridge) and [Sky Bridge tour](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/enjoy/skyBridge) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026. The winter closure notice is on the tour page.

- **Booking:** online booking opens one month before and **can't be used for the same day**. Seoul Sky recommends booking online in advance; on the day, the B1 and 117F counters sell only places left over from online sales.
- **Who can go:** height **140 cm or more** and weight **under 120 kg**. On age, the operator's page gives two versions — its summary box says 14 and over, while its notes say 12 and over, with a legal guardian's consent needed under 14 — so confirm the age rule when you book. Up to 12 people per tour.
- **It's a climb:** the route includes stairs from the 121st floor up to the bridge, about 50 m vertically. The operator says it may refuse people who have been drinking, and lists pregnant women, people with heart, blood-vessel or spinal disc conditions, older visitors and people with limited sight among those the tour is restricted for.
- **It closes in winter.** The Sky Bridge tour page announces a winter closure from **November 30, 2026, to February 28, 2027** (the observatory itself stays open). The price page still shows last winter's dates, so check the operator's latest notice before you plan.

## One day in Jamsil

| When | What |
|---|---|
| 10:00 | Lotte World Adventure opens. Do the outdoor Magic Island rides early if the weather is good |
| Afternoon | Indoor Adventure area, parades and shows |
| Around sunset | Walk to Lotte World Tower and go up Seoul Sky for the day-to-night view |
| Evening | Dinner in Jamsil, then the subway on Line 2 or 8 |

Prefer a shorter park visit? An **After 4** park ticket (₩52,000 for adults) with Seoul Sky in the morning works too — just remember Seoul Sky opens at 10:30.

Source: [Lotte World Adventure — tickets and hours](https://adventure.lotteworld.com/usage-guide/service/closed) and [Seoul Sky — hours](https://seoulsky.lotteworld.com/guide/hours) (Korean); checked Oct 29, 2026. The timings in the plan are our suggestion.

Getting around: see our [Seoul subway guide](/seoul-subway-guide/) and [T-money card guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/), or plan the route with [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/). For more ideas, see the [Seoul 3, 4 or 5-day itinerary](/seoul-itinerary-3-4-5-days/) and [N Seoul Tower](/n-seoul-tower-guide/), Seoul's other big viewpoint.

## Before you go

1. Check **that day's hours** on both official calendars — they change by date.
2. Arrive at least **one hour before closing** — that's when ticket sales and entry end.
3. Want the Magic Pass? Open the **Lotte World app at 08:30** on the day — it can sell out.
4. Want the Sky Bridge? Check the **height, weight and age limits**, book online ahead if you can (same-day places are only what's left on site), and note the winter closure from Nov 30, 2026, to Feb 28, 2027.
5. Buying a combined ticket? You need a **physical ticket** — a screenshot won't work.

## FAQ

### How much is a Lotte World ticket?

A 1-day park ticket is ₩64,000 for adults (19+), ₩56,000 for ages 13–18 and ₩49,000 for ages 3–12. From 4 p.m. it's ₩52,000, ₩45,000 and ₩38,000. A combined ticket with the Folk Museum costs a little more (₩67,000 for adults).

### How much is Seoul Sky?

₩33,000 for ages 13 and over and ₩29,000 for children from 36 months to 12. Under 36 months are free with a guardian. The Sky Bridge tour is extra: ₩130,000 including admission, with height, weight and age limits.

### What time does Lotte World close?

It changes by date. On the days we checked, it closed at 21:00 or 22:00, and ticket sales and entry ended one hour earlier. Check the calendar on the official site for your date.

### Is Lotte World indoors?

Mostly. The main Adventure area is under a glass dome. Magic Island is outdoors on Seokchon Lake, and some rides there can stop in cold, heat, wind or rain.

### Is the Magic Pass worth it?

It costs ₩54,000–₩80,000 for five rides on top of your ticket, sells only in the app from 08:30 on the day (Premium can be booked ahead), and sells out. It's worth it if you're there on a busy day and want the big rides without long waits.
