# Taxis in Korea: Fares, Apps and How to Get One

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/taxis-in-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-25

## Quick answer

- A regular taxi in Seoul starts at ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km by day, then ₩100 per 131 m, plus ₩100 per 30 seconds when the taxi is moving below 15.72 km/h. Late at night the base fare rises to ₩5,800–₩6,700.
- Regular taxis use the meter; pay with cash, a credit card or a transit card. The Korea Tourism Organization says most taxis don't require tips.
- Don't speak Korean? Use a taxi app with English (k.ride, Uber or TABA), or book an International Taxi with English-speaking drivers at least 24 hours ahead.

**A regular taxi in Seoul costs ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km by day, then ₩100 for every 131 m, and between 10 PM and 4 AM a late-night surcharge of 20–40% applies.** You pay by the meter with cash, a credit card or a transit card, and most taxis don't expect a tip. If you don't speak Korean, call one with an app that works in English (k.ride, Uber or TABA), or book an International Taxi, whose drivers speak English, Chinese and Japanese.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — taxi fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/), [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxi](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) and [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr); checked Oct 25, 2026.

![Graphic: taxis in Korea at a glance — Seoul fares, night surcharge, apps, International Taxi, paying](/img/taxi-steps.png?v=c0228184 "Taxis in Korea at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Regular taxi (Seoul, day) | ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km, then ₩100 per 131 m, plus ₩100 per 30 seconds below 15.72 km/h |
| Late night (10 PM–4 AM) | Base fare ₩5,800–₩6,700, with a 20–40% surcharge |
| Paying | Cash, credit card or transit card · regular taxis use the meter · most taxis don't require tips |
| Apps in English | k.ride (Kakao Mobility), Uber, TABA |
| English-speaking drivers | International Taxi: book online at least 24 hours ahead, or ask at the desk at Incheon Airport |
| Incheon Airport → Seoul | International Taxi zone fares from ₩70,000 to ₩95,000 by sedan |

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/) (fares as of Feb 1, 2023), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661), [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr) and [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); checked Oct 25, 2026.

## Which taxi is which

![An orange taxi with a roof sign driving past a tree-lined street in Seoul](/img/photo-seoul-taxi.jpg?v=e7179087 "A taxi in downtown Seoul. Photo: Joshua T. Garcia (CC0), cropped.")

| Type | How to spot it | Good to know |
|---|---|---|
| **Regular taxi** | Yellow license plate and a roof sign that reads "TAXI" | The cheapest metered taxi |
| **Deluxe taxi** | Usually black, larger or more expensive cars | Higher fares (see below) |
| **International Taxi** | Booked in advance or at the airport desk | Drivers speak English, Chinese or Japanese; 20% surcharge on the meter |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxi](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) and [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr); checked Oct 25, 2026.

## Seoul taxi fares

Regular street taxis use the meter, and the final fare is rounded to ₩10; tolls are added at the actual amount. Approved fixed-fare services, including International Taxi's airport zone fares, use a different fare plan, so check the fare plan when booking.

| Seoul, as of Feb 1, 2023 | Regular (sedan) taxi | SUV, van and deluxe taxi |
|---|---|---|
| Daytime base fare | ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km | ₩7,000 for the first 3.0 km |
| Distance fare | ₩100 per 131 m | ₩200 per 151 m |
| Time fare (slow traffic) | ₩100 per 30 seconds | ₩200 per 36 seconds |
| Late-night base fare | ₩5,800 (10–11 PM, 2–4 AM) · ₩6,700 (11 PM–2 AM) | ₩8,400 |
| Late-night surcharge | 20% (10–11 PM, 2–4 AM) · 40% (11 PM–2 AM) | 20% (10 PM–4 AM) |
| Outside the taxi's licensed service area | +20%, up to 60% in total late at night | +20% |

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — taxi fares](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/); checked Oct 25, 2026.

Regular sedans combine distance and time charges at low speed; the SUV, van and deluxe calculation uses different rules.

A 20% out-of-area surcharge can apply to Seoul taxis outside their licensed service area. Joint service areas are exceptions: Seoul's rules say Incheon and Gimpo airports, Gwangmyeong and Wirye New Town count as Seoul's service area (Bokjeong Station's transfer center excepted), so a Seoul taxi shouldn't add this surcharge just for crossing the city boundary to Incheon Airport. Check the meter and receipt for any surcharge.

Source: [Seoul Metropolitan Government — taxi service areas](https://news.seoul.go.kr/traffic/archives/34700) (Korean); checked Oct 25, 2026.

**Outside Seoul**, base fares differ by region, and the base distance and surcharges vary locally. For regular taxis by day, the Korea Tourism Organization lists ₩4,800 in Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi-do and Gwangju; ₩4,500 in Daegu and Ulsan; ₩4,600 in Gangwon State; and ₩4,300 in Daejeon and Jeju.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxi](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) (page updated Jan 22, 2026); checked Oct 25, 2026.

## How to get a taxi

1. **Hail one on the street**, or go to a **taxi stand**. Stands are at busy places such as bus terminals and major subway stations. In Seoul, you can call +82-2-120 to ask where the nearest stand is.
2. **Or call one with an app.** You see a fare estimate before you ride, but there may be a small call fee on top of the fare.

| App | What the official pages say |
|---|---|
| **k.ride** | Kakao Mobility's version of Kakao T for visitors: English, Chinese and Japanese; sign in with Google or Apple; register an overseas credit card |
| **Uber** | Use the Uber app you already have to call an Uber Taxi; messages to the driver are translated automatically |
| **TABA** | Address search in any language; Visa, Mastercard, UnionPay and JCB; covers Seoul and nearby areas, Incheon, Jeju, Chuncheon, Wonju, Daejeon, Gumi, Gwangju, Gimhae and Changwon |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxi](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) and [TABA](https://www.tabataxi.app/); checked Oct 25, 2026.

> **Local tip:** If you book through TABA, the app charges your card automatically. TABA warns that paying the driver in cash as well means you pay twice.

## International Taxi: English-speaking drivers

International Taxi is a taxi service designated by Seoul City, with drivers who speak English, Chinese and Japanese.

| | |
|---|---|
| Booking | Online at intltaxi.co.kr at least 24 hours ahead, or the information booth at Incheon Airport Terminal 1 or 2 · phone 1644-2255 |
| Within Seoul | Meter fare + 20% |
| Incheon Airport → Seoul | Fixed zone fares (below) |
| Paying | Cash (won) or credit card (Visa, Amex, Mastercard) |

| Zone (Seoul districts) | Sedan | SUV, van, deluxe |
|---|---|---|
| A: Gangseo | ₩70,000 | ₩100,000 |
| B: Yangcheon, Guro, Yeongdeungpo, Mapo, Eunpyeong, Seodaemun | ₩75,000 | ₩110,000 |
| C: Geumcheon, Gwanak, Dongjak, Yongsan, Jung, Jongno | ₩85,000 | ₩120,000 |
| D: Seocho, Gangnam, Seongdong, Dongdaemun, Seongbuk, Gangbuk | ₩90,000 | ₩130,000 |
| E: Songpa, Gangdong, Gwangjin, Jungnang, Nowon, Dobong | ₩95,000 | ₩140,000 |

Source: [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr), [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/) and [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661); checked Oct 25, 2026. For the train and bus from the airport, see [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/).

> **Our take:** A regular taxi is the cheapest metered option. An International Taxi costs more, but it's worth it if you need an English-speaking driver or a fixed price from the airport.

## Paying

- Regular street taxis normally use the meter; approved fixed-fare services use their booked fare plan. Tips are generally not expected.
- You can pay with **cash, a credit card or a transit card** such as T-money (see our [T-money guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/)).
- Check the meter and receipt for late-night or out-of-area surcharges.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Taxi](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661) and [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/); checked Oct 25, 2026. More on cards: [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).

## Before you ride

1. Install a taxi app that works in English (k.ride, Uber or TABA) and add your card.
2. Save your hotel's address in Korean to show the driver.
3. Need an English-speaking driver from the airport? Book an International Taxi at least 24 hours ahead.
4. Riding after 10 PM? Expect a 20–40% late-night surcharge in Seoul.
5. Keep a little won or a transit card as a backup way to pay.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140661), [International Taxi](https://www.intltaxi.co.kr) and [Seoul Metropolitan Government](https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/); checked Oct 25, 2026.

## FAQ

### How much is a taxi in Seoul?

A regular taxi costs ₩4,800 for the first 1.6 km by day, then ₩100 per 131 m, plus ₩100 per 30 seconds when moving below 15.72 km/h. Between 10 PM and 4 AM, a late-night surcharge of 20–40% applies.

### Can I pay for a taxi in Korea with a credit card?

Yes. Taxis accept cash, credit cards and transit cards. Apps such as k.ride and TABA also take overseas cards registered in the app.

### Do you tip taxi drivers in Korea?

Tips are generally not expected. The Korea Tourism Organization says most taxis charge by the meter and don't require tips.

### How much is a taxi from Incheon Airport to Seoul?

An International Taxi charges a fixed zone fare from ₩70,000 to ₩95,000 by sedan, depending on the district. A regular taxi uses the meter, plus tolls.

### Is there a taxi app in English in Korea?

Yes. k.ride (Kakao Mobility's app for visitors) works in English, Chinese and Japanese; Uber translates your messages to the driver; and TABA lets you search addresses in any language.

## Sources

- Seoul Metropolitan Government — Taxi fares: https://english.seoul.go.kr/policy/transportation/modes-of-transport/taxi/

# Busan Travel Guide: Beaches, Gamcheon Village and Jagalchi Market

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/busan-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Busan is Korea's big seaside city. Start with Haeundae Beach, Gamcheon Culture Village and Jagalchi Market, one of Korea's largest seafood markets.
- Get there by KTX: Seoul to Busan via Gyeongju is ₩54,400 (standard adult), or ₩52,900 from Suseo; fares differ by route. In the city, the subway costs ₩1,600 or ₩1,800 by transit card.
- Eat dwaeji gukbap (pork and rice soup). A Visit Busan food guide puts it first, followed by milmyeon (wheat noodles).

**Busan's three starter sights are Haeundae Beach (free, about 1.5 km of sand), Gamcheon Culture Village (free, open daily) and Jagalchi Market (main building closed on the 1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesdays).** From Seoul Station, the KTX via Gyeongju costs ₩54,400 (adult standard class; fares vary by route), and the city subway costs ₩1,600 or ₩1,800 by transit card. The dish to try is dwaeji gukbap, pork and rice soup.

Below: each sight in a table, what to eat, transport and a two-day plan.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=111053), [Visit Busan](https://www.visitbusan.net/index.do?menuCd=DOM_000000301001001000&uc_seq=365&lang_cd=en), [Busan Infrastructure Corporation](https://www.bisco.or.kr/jagalchimarket/sub/sub02/sub02_1/?tabName=con04), [Busan Transportation Corporation](https://www.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040101) and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

![Graphic: Busan at a glance — KTX from Seoul, Haeundae, Gamcheon, Jagalchi, pork and rice soup](/img/busan-steps.png?v=2ceb6379 "Busan at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Getting there | KTX Seoul–Busan via Gyeongju ₩54,400, Suseo–Busan ₩52,900 (standard adult; fares differ by route) |
| Getting around | Subway ₩1,600 or ₩1,800 by transit card, depending on distance; T-money works |
| Beach | Haeundae Beach, free, about 1.5 km of sand |
| Village | Gamcheon Culture Village, free, open daily |
| Market | Jagalchi Market; main building closed on the 1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesdays |
| Must-eat | Dwaeji gukbap (pork and rice soup), milmyeon (wheat noodles) |

Source: [Visit Busan](https://www.visitbusan.net/index.do?menuCd=DOM_000000301001001000&uc_seq=365&lang_cd=en), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=111053), [Busan Infrastructure Corporation](https://www.bisco.or.kr/jagalchimarket/sub/sub02/sub02_1/?tabName=con04), [Busan Transportation Corporation](https://www.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040101) and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026; see our [KTX guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/)); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Haeundae Beach

![Waves rolling onto the sand at Haeundae Beach, with open sea behind](/img/photo-busan-haeundae-sea.jpg?v=634c786a "Haeundae Beach, April 2025. Photo: Vichycombo (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

The Korea Tourism Organization calls Haeundae the most famous beach in Busan, with white sand in front of a shallow bay. It gets crowded every summer.

| | |
|---|---|
| Entry | Free |
| Size | About 1.5 km long and 30–50 m wide |
| Nearby | Dongbaekseom Island, Busan Aquarium |
| Swimming | Depends on the season and on-site rules: check the signs at the beach |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Haeundae Beach](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=111053); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Gamcheon Culture Village

![Colorful houses stacked up a green hillside at Gamcheon Culture Village](/img/photo-busan-gamcheon.jpg?v=0df97420 "Gamcheon Culture Village, April 2026. Photo: VN.NguyenDucDuy (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Refugees settled this hillside during the Korean War. In 2009, students, artists and residents decorated it as part of a village art project, and it became known as "the Machu Picchu of Korea."

| | |
|---|---|
| Entry | Free (parking is charged) |
| Open | Every day · 09:00–18:00 (March–October) · 09:00–17:00 (November–February) |
| Getting there | Subway Line 1 to Toseong Station, Exit 6 → village bus Saha 1-1, Seo-gu 2 or Seo-gu 2-2 → Gamjeong Elementary School, then about a 5-minute walk |
| Do | Buy a stamp map at the village information center and follow it through the alleys |

Source: [Visit Busan — Gamcheon Culture Village](https://www.visitbusan.net/index.do?menuCd=DOM_000000301001001000&uc_seq=365&lang_cd=en); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** People live here. Visit Busan asks visitors to keep quiet and keep it clean, and drones aren't allowed.

## Jagalchi Market

![Fish stalls and shoppers along an indoor aisle at Jagalchi Market](/img/photo-busan-jagalchi.jpg?v=4b139ec0 "Jagalchi Market, October 2022. Photo: Bernard Gagnon (CC0), cropped.")

One of the largest seafood markets in Korea, selling both live and dried fish, and you can eat fresh raw fish right at the market. Most of the sellers are women, known as the Jagalchi *ajumeoni*.

| | |
|---|---|
| Hours | 05:00–22:00, as listed by the Korea Tourism Organization; individual stalls and restaurants keep their own hours |
| Closed | Main market building: 1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesdays of the month |
| Eat | Raw fish and seafood at the market |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Jagalchi Market](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=69318) and [Busan Infrastructure Corporation — Jagalchi Market](https://www.bisco.or.kr/jagalchimarket/sub/sub02/sub02_1/?tabName=con04); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What to eat

| Dish | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Dwaeji gukbap** | Pork and rice soup: hot pork-bone broth served as a set with chive kimchi, salted shrimp and noodles |
| **Milmyeon** | Busan's wheat noodles |
| **Raw fish and seafood** | At Jagalchi Market |

A Visit Busan food guide puts dwaeji gukbap first among the city's foods and milmyeon second.

Source: [Visit Busan — Delicious Busan](https://visitbusan.net/index.do?lang_cd=en&menuCd=DOM_000000302003001000&uc_seq=1008) and [Korea Tourism Organization — Jagalchi Market](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=69318); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Dwaeji gukbap is made with pork bones. If you avoid pork or have other dietary needs, ask about the ingredients before you order.

## Getting there and around

| | |
|---|---|
| KTX from Seoul Station | ₩54,400 via Gyeongju (standard adult) |
| KTX from Suseo Station | ₩52,900 (standard adult) |
| Subway in Busan | ₩1,600 or ₩1,800 by transit card, by distance; a single QR ticket costs a little more |
| Card | T-money works on Busan's subway: see our [T-money guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/) |
| Routes | Plan each trip in [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) |

KTX fares differ by route, so check the fare of the train you pick when booking. Our [KTX booking guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) shows how to buy tickets in English.

Source: Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026) and [Busan Transportation Corporation — fares](https://www.humetro.busan.kr/homepage/english/page/subLocation.do?menu_no=100601040101); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## A two-day plan

> **Our take:** Gamcheon (which Visit Busan calls a landmark of west Busan) and Jagalchi in Jung-gu fit well on one day. Give Haeundae its own afternoon and evening.

| Day | Where |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Gamcheon Culture Village → Jagalchi Market for a seafood meal |
| Day 2 | Haeundae Beach, then dwaeji gukbap for dinner |

## Before you go

1. Book your KTX to Busan (Seoul Station or Suseo) and check the fare for your train.
2. Bring a transit card such as T-money for the subway and village buses.
3. Install Naver Map for routes between sights.
4. Check that the Jagalchi main building isn't closed that day (1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesdays).
5. Save the Busan travel hotline: 1330.

Source: [Busan Infrastructure Corporation — Jagalchi Market](https://www.bisco.or.kr/jagalchimarket/sub/sub02/sub02_1/?tabName=con04) and [Visit Busan](https://www.visitbusan.net/index.do?menuCd=DOM_000000301001001000&uc_seq=365&lang_cd=en); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### How do I get from Seoul to Busan?

By KTX. A standard adult ticket from Seoul Station via Gyeongju costs ₩54,400, or ₩52,900 from Suseo Station. Fares differ by route, so check your train when booking.

### Is Gamcheon Culture Village free?

Yes. Entry is free (parking is charged), and it's open daily: 09:00–18:00 from March to October and 09:00–17:00 from November to February.

### When is Jagalchi Market closed?

The main market building is closed on the 1st, 3rd and 5th Tuesdays of the month.

### What food is Busan famous for?

A Visit Busan food guide puts dwaeji gukbap (pork and rice soup) first, followed by milmyeon (wheat noodles). Jagalchi Market is known for seafood.

### How much is the Busan subway?

₩1,600 or ₩1,800 for an adult with a transit card, depending on distance.

# Gyeongju Travel Guide: Korea's Ancient Silla Capital in One Day

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/gyeongju-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years. Two UNESCO listings cover its Silla heritage: the Gyeongju Historic Areas and Seokguram Grotto with Bulguksa Temple.
- Get there by KTX from Seoul Station (adult standard-class fare example ₩44,500; fares vary by route), then use Naver Map for buses or taxis between sites.
- Save Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond for the evening. It's open 09:00–22:00 (last entry 21:30); adults pay ₩3,000.

**Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom (57 BCE–935 CE), and its Silla sites are covered by two UNESCO World Heritage listings (1995 and 2000).** Start with four sights: Bulguksa Temple, the Daereungwon tombs, Cheomseongdae and Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond (open until 22:00, adults ₩3,000). From Seoul Station, the KTX adult standard-class fare example is ₩44,500.

The Korea Tourism Organization calls Gyeongju "a living museum." Below: each sight in a table, English guiding, transport and a one-day plan.

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=94404) and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

![Graphic: Gyeongju at a glance — Silla capital, UNESCO sites, KTX from Seoul, Donggung Palace at night](/img/gyeongju-steps.png?v=c181dd5b "Gyeongju at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Why go | Capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years (57 BCE–935 CE) |
| UNESCO (Silla) | Gyeongju Historic Areas (2000); Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple (1995) |
| Getting there | KTX from Seoul Station; adult standard-class fare example ₩44,500 (fares vary by route) |
| Top sights | Bulguksa Temple · Daereungwon tombs · Cheomseongdae · Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond |
| At night | Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond, open until 22:00 |
| English guiding | Walk-in sessions at major sites; ask on site (lunch break 12:00–13:00) |

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=534028) and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026; see our [KTX guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/)); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Why Gyeongju matters

UNESCO dates the Silla dynasty from 57 BCE to 935 CE, and says the sites in and around Gyeongju "bear outstanding testimony" to its achievements. This guide focuses on the two World Heritage listings tied to Silla:

| UNESCO listing | Inscribed | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| **Gyeongju Historic Areas** | 2000 | Five areas in and around the city: royal tombs, the old palace grounds with Cheomseongdae and Wolji Pond, and Buddhist sites on Mount Namsan |
| **Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple** | 1995 | An 8th-century grotto with a monumental stone Buddha looking toward the sea, and Bulguksa Temple, built in 774 |

Gyeongju also has a part in two other listings: **Yangdong Village** belongs to the Historic Villages of Korea (2010), and **Oksan Seowon** is one of the Seowon, Korean Neo-Confucian Academies (2019).

Source: UNESCO — [Gyeongju Historic Areas](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976), [Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/736), [Hahoe and Yangdong](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1324) and [Seowon](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1498); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Where to start

### Bulguksa Temple

![The stone staircases leading up to a gate at Bulguksa Temple, with flower beds in front](/img/photo-gyeongju-bulguksa.jpg?v=687aa9c8 "The entrance stairs at Bulguksa Temple, June 2024. Photo: Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

The Korea Tourism Organization calls Bulguksa one of Korea's most iconic Buddhist temples.

| | |
|---|---|
| Built | 774 |
| Don't miss | The Seokgatap and Dabotap pagodas (national treasures) |
| Nearby | Seokguram Grotto, on the slopes of Mount Toham, listed with it by UNESCO |
| Where | On the edge of the city: check the bus or taxi route in Naver Map |

### Daereungwon Tomb Complex and Cheomseongdae

![Grassy royal burial mounds at the Daereungwon Tomb Complex in Gyeongju](/img/photo-gyeongju-daereungwon.jpg?v=08b93fc4 "Daereungwon Tomb Complex, October 2022. Photo: Bernard Gagnon (CC0), cropped.")

In the middle of town, the Silla royal tombs rise as rounded green mounds. UNESCO notes that excavations revealed rich grave goods of gold, glass and fine ceramics.

| | |
|---|---|
| Go inside | Cheonmachong, the tomb in Daereungwon open to the public, displays Silla-era artifacts including a golden crown |
| Walk on to | Cheomseongdae Observatory, part of the same Wolseong area as the old palace site and Wolji Pond |

### Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond

![Donggung Palace pavilion lit up at dusk and reflected in Wolji Pond](/img/photo-gyeongju-donggung-wolji.jpg?v=9fd4e1ef "Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at blue hour, June 2024. Photo: Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

A secondary palace of the Silla court, used for banquets and important guests. The pond was dug in 674; its name, Wolji, means "a pond that reflects the moon."

| | |
|---|---|
| Open | 09:00–22:00, all year (last entry 21:30) |
| Admission | Adults ₩3,000 · teenagers ₩2,000 · children ₩1,000 |
| Best time | Sunset, when the pavilions are lit and reflected in the water |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Gyeongju course](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=534028) and [Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=94404); [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/976); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Admission at temples and tomb sites has changed in recent years, and figures online often disagree. Check each site's official visitor information before you go instead of relying on an old blog post.

## English guiding

Walk-in cultural guiding is offered at major heritage sites, including Bulguksa, Daereungwon and Donggung Palace, from the "Korean Culture & Tourism Guide" office near each entrance.

- **When:** sessions generally start on the hour from 10:00 to 16:00, with a lunch break from 12:00 to 13:00. Schedules can change.
- **How:** ask at the guide office for that day's English session. No reservation is needed.
- **Bulguksa on Sundays:** the city's regular guide roster doesn't cover Bulguksa on Sundays, so confirm there in advance.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Gyeongju course](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/hdrdslt/hdrdsltView.do?crsSn=534028) and Gyeongju City's cultural guide information; checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Getting there and around

| | |
|---|---|
| From Seoul | KTX from Seoul Station to Gyeongju · adult standard-class fare example ₩44,500 · fares vary by route, so check the fare of the train you choose · [how to book](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) |
| Between sites | Sights are spread out: put each stop into [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) for the bus or taxi route |
| Paying | Bring a card and a little cash: see [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/) |

Source: Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## A one-day plan

> **Our take:** This order keeps the night view for last. Book a return train that leaves you time after dark.

| Time | Where | Why then |
|---|---|---|
| Morning | Bulguksa Temple | It's on the edge of the city: go first |
| Afternoon | Daereungwon and Cheomseongdae | Both in the middle of town, close together |
| Evening | Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond | Lit up after sunset; last entry 21:30 |

## Before you go

1. Book your KTX from Seoul Station to Gyeongju and check the fare for your train.
2. Install Naver Map for buses and taxis between sites.
3. Plan Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond for the evening (last entry 21:30).
4. Bring a little cash and a card.
5. Want an English guide? Ask at the guide office near the site entrance; at Bulguksa on a Sunday, confirm in advance.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=94404) and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### Why is Gyeongju famous?

It was the capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years. Its Silla heritage is covered by two UNESCO listings: the Gyeongju Historic Areas and Seokguram Grotto with Bulguksa Temple.

### How do I get from Seoul to Gyeongju?

By KTX from Seoul Station. An adult standard-class fare example is ₩44,500; fares vary by route, so check the fare of the train you choose when booking.

### Is Gyeongju worth a day trip?

In our view, a full day covers Bulguksa, the royal tombs and Donggung Palace at night. Staying overnight gives you more time for Seokguram and the other historic areas.

### Are there English tours in Gyeongju?

Yes, walk-in guiding is offered at major heritage sites. Sessions generally start on the hour from 10:00 to 16:00 (not 12:00–13:00); ask at the guide office for that day's English session.

### What time does Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond close?

It's open from 09:00 to 22:00, with last entry at 21:30.

# How to Book KTX Train Tickets in Korea as a Foreigner

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/how-to-book-ktx-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Book in English on Korail's official site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng) or in the KORAIL+ app. The normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time) two months before your travel date; Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains follow a separate schedule.
- KTX and SRT merged on September 1, 2026. The government says they now run as KTX, with fares on average 10% lower than before. Seoul–Busan (via Gyeongju) is ₩54,400 in standard class.
- Keep your email and password — that's how you look up a ticket booked on the foreigner site, and you'll need them to cancel online before departure.

![A blue KTX-Cheongryong high-speed train waiting at a platform at Seoul Station](/img/photo-ktx-seoul-station.jpg?v=326e9396 "A KTX-Cheongryong train at Seoul Station, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

**Book the KTX in English on Korail's site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng) or in the KORAIL+ app, and pay by credit card online. Tickets normally go on sale at 07:00 Korea time two months before your travel date** (Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains follow a separate schedule). Since September 1, 2026, the KTX and the SRT run as one service called KTX, so a blog post that sends you to a separate SRT website is out of date. A standard-class adult fare from Seoul to Busan via Gyeongju is ₩54,400; fares vary by route.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets), [Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148970889) (Korean) and [Korail — KTX fare table, as of Sep 1, 2026](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Where to book | Korail's site for foreigners (korail.com/global/eng), the KORAIL+ app, ticket machines or station counters — not at subway stations |
| When tickets go on sale | Normally from 07:00 (Korea time), two months before your travel date — holiday trains differ |
| How to pay | Credit card (online) |
| Finding your ticket | The email address and password you used when booking |
| Cancelling | Online before departure; after departure, generally at a station counter (see the KORAIL+ exception below) |

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What changed in September 2026

Korea used to have two high-speed operators: Korail ran the KTX, and a separate company, SR, ran the SRT from Suseo Station. After the companies were merged, the government says the two started running as KTX from September 1, 2026. Three things matter for visitors:

- **One place to book.** Integrated trains are booked through the KORAIL+ app and the Korail website. KORAIL+ replaced Korail's old app, Korail Talk.
- **Lower fares.** The government says KTX fares were brought down to former SRT levels — about 10% lower on average.
- **More seats on trains from Suseo.** Most of the added trains run on the Suseo routes, which the government says have about 30% more seats.

Source: [Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, Aug 31, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148970889) and [Aug 3, 2026](https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148969267) (Korean); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How much a KTX ticket costs

These are adult standard-class fares from Korail's official KTX fare table, effective September 1, 2026:

| Route | Standard class |
|---|---|
| Seoul – Busan (via Gyeongju) | ₩54,400 |
| Suseo – Busan | ₩52,900 |
| Seoul – Dongdaegu (Daegu) | ₩39,000 |
| Seoul – Gyeongju | ₩44,500 |
| Seoul – Daejeon | ₩21,600 |
| Yongsan – Gwangju Songjeong | ₩42,000 |
| Yongsan – Jeonju | ₩31,600 |
| Yongsan – Yeosu EXPO | ₩45,400 |

Fares vary by route — the same two cities can have different fares depending on the stops a train makes — so check the price shown when you book. Korail's table also notes that the 10% reduction was set for three years and may be adjusted later.

![Rows of grey standard-class seats inside a KTX-Cheongryong carriage](/img/photo-ktx-standard-class.jpg?v=b1b9743d "Standard class on a KTX-Cheongryong train, 2024. Photo: 생각하는 나무 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Source: [Korail — KTX fare table, as of Sep 1, 2026](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/train-timeTable) (Korean, Excel download); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Booking online, in English

![Booking a KTX ticket in four steps: open Korail's English site or the KORAIL+ app, search, save your email and password, pay by credit card](/img/ktx-steps.png?v=a7f9ef86 "Booking in four steps. Details below.")

1. Go to **korail.com/global/eng** — Korail's official site for foreigners. (The old letskorail.com address now redirects to korail.com.)
2. Search your departure station, arrival station, date and number of passengers, and pick a train.
3. Enter an email address and a password. Korail says you need to type them exactly — including upper- and lower-case letters — to look up your ticket later, and suggests writing them down.
4. Pay by credit card.
5. To check or cancel, open **MY TICKET** and enter the same email and password.

Source: [Korail — official site for foreigners](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/main) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Save the email and password in your phone's notes the moment you book. Without them you can't pull up the ticket on the foreigner site.

## When tickets go on sale

Korail says the normal booking window opens at **07:00 (Korea time), two months before** the departure date. Online, you can buy until the train leaves; ticket machines stop selling 10 minutes before departure, and station counters sell until departure.

The big exception is Korea's two main holidays. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can have their own reservation schedule and rules — for Chuseok 2026, Korail ran a separate booking period that required membership, then opened remaining seats later, when non-members could buy and pay straight away. Check Korail's latest holiday notice if you're travelling around those dates.

> **Our take:** For Friday-to-Sunday trips, book as soon as your normal booking window opens. Those are also the days with higher cancellation fees, so pick your train with care.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets) and [2026 Chuseok reservations notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/25622); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Buying at the station

![Korail ticket counters, ticket machines and departure boards at Pyeongtaek Station](/img/photo-korail-ticket-counter.jpg?v=00f643af "Korail ticket counters and machines at Pyeongtaek Station, 2024. Photo: MNXANL (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

You can also buy at ticket machines or the counter in a train station. Note that this means a railway station — Korail says KTX tickets aren't sold at subway stations.

Source: [Korail — ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## If your plans change

Before departure, you can cancel online — in MY TICKET for tickets booked on Korail's English website. After the train has left, the English guide directs you to a station counter. Korail's Korean guide also lists an exception: KTX tickets bought through KORAIL+ can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure, if it's confirmed that you're not on the train. Follow the refund options for the channel you bought from. Refunds aren't possible after the arrival time printed on the ticket.

The fee depends on when you cancel and on the day of travel. "The day before" means the previous calendar date, not a rolling 24-hour period:

| When you cancel | Mon–Thu trains (excluding public holidays and designated holiday periods) | Fri–Sun, public holidays, Seollal and Chuseok |
|---|---|---|
| From booking until 2 days before departure | No fee | Minimum fee |
| The day before departure | No fee | 5% |
| On the departure date, until 3 hours before | No fee | 10% |
| Less than 3 hours before departure | 5% | 20% |
| Up to 20 minutes after departure | 15% | 30% |
| 20 to 60 minutes after departure | 40% | 40% |
| 60 minutes after departure until arrival | 70% | 70% |

Korail's Korean guide lists the minimum fee as ₩400.

Source: [Korail — purchase and refund guide](https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay) (Korean) and [ticketing guide](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/tickets); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Is the KORAIL PASS worth it?

The KORAIL PASS is a rail pass for foreign visitors. The current select passes let you choose 2, 3, 4 or 5 travel days within a 10-day period from the pass's starting date:

| Pass | Adult (13+) | Child (6–12) |
|---|---|---|
| 2-day select | ₩131,000 | ₩66,000 |
| 3-day select | ₩186,000 | ₩93,000 |
| 4-day select | ₩234,000 | ₩117,000 |
| 5-day select | ₩275,000 | ₩138,000 |

You need a valid passport and a credit card to buy it, and the details must match your passport. Choose your travel dates in MY TICKET before reserving seats; seat reservations open two months before departure, up to two seat tickets per person per day. Board with your pass, your passport and, if you reserved one, your seat reservation. Refunds are possible only before the pass's starting date.

Korail's current pass guide lists metropolitan railways and temporary tourist trains as not included. An older notice from 2024 also excluded SRT trains, which have run as KTX since September 2026. If your plans use trains from Suseo Station, check that a seat reservation is available for that train when you book, or ask Korail's call center (+82-1599-7777).

Source: [Korail — About KORAIL PASS](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/korailpass), [pass reservation](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/korailpass/reservation) and [older pass notice](https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/18801); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** Do the sums for your own trip. A 2-day pass costs ₩131,000, while a Seoul–Busan return in standard class is ₩108,800 (₩54,400 each way via Gyeongju) — so for one return trip, regular tickets are cheaper. A pass can make sense when you're fitting several long trips into a short window.

## Before you travel

1. Decide your stations — trains to Busan leave from Seoul Station and Suseo Station, among others.
2. Book from 07:00 (Korea time) two months ahead for weekend trips — and check Korail's holiday notice if you're travelling around Seollal or Chuseok.
3. Save your booking email and password.
4. Check you'll have data on the day for the app or your ticket — see [eSIM vs SIM card vs pocket Wi-Fi](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/).
5. Plan the trip to the station: [how to use Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) and [how to get a T-money card](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/).

## FAQ

### Can foreigners book KTX tickets online?

Yes. Korail runs an English site for foreigners at korail.com/global/eng, and tickets can also be bought in the KORAIL+ app, at ticket machines and at station counters.

### How far in advance can I book the KTX?

Korail's normal booking window opens at 07:00 (Korea time), two months before the departure date. Seollal and Chuseok holiday trains can follow a separate schedule.

### How much is the KTX from Seoul to Busan?

₩54,400 for an adult in standard class from Seoul Station via Gyeongju, and ₩52,900 from Suseo Station, according to Korail's fare table effective September 1, 2026. Other routes between the two cities can cost a different amount.

### Is the SRT still separate from the KTX?

No. The government says the KTX and SRT started running as one KTX service on September 1, 2026, with integrated trains booked through KORAIL+ and the Korail website.

### Can I get a refund on a KTX ticket?

Yes. Before departure you can cancel online; after departure, generally at a station counter (KORAIL+ KTX tickets can be refunded in the app up to 10 minutes after departure if you're not on the train). No refunds after arrival. Fees depend on timing and the day of travel. For non-holiday Monday–Thursday departures, cancellation more than three hours before departure is free. Public holidays and the designated Seollal/Chuseok travel periods use the holiday fee schedule.

## Sources

- Korail — KORAIL PASS reservation: https://www.korail.com/global/eng/korailpass/reservation
- Korail — About KORAIL PASS (pricing, 10-day validity, how to reserve seats): https://www.korail.com/global/eng/passengerGuide/ticketTypes/korailpass
- Korail — Ticket purchase, refund and penalties (Korean): https://www.korail.com/ticket/reserve/guide/pay

- Korail — KORAIL PASS information (older notice, Nov 2024): https://www.korail.com/global/eng/siteInfo/notice/18801

- Korea Policy Briefing — Korail–SR merger approved, KORAIL+ app launched (Aug 3, 2026, Korean): https://www.korea.kr/news/policyNewsView.do?newsId=148969267

# Jeju Island Travel Guide: Volcanoes, Hallasan and Black Pork

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/jeju-travel-guide/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Jeju is Korea's volcanic island. UNESCO lists Seongsan Ilchulbong, Mount Halla (Hallasan) and the Geomunoreum lava tubes as a World Natural Heritage site (2007).
- Hiking to the top of Hallasan? Book, bring ID and start early. The two summit trails, Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa, run on reservations, and summit-route checkpoints close at 11:30 (Oct–Mar) or 12:30 (Apr–Sep).
- Get around by bus with a transit card: ₩1,150 on regular buses; express buses start at ₩2,000 and charge the rest when you tap off.

**Jeju is a volcanic island whose three main natural sites, Seongsan Ilchulbong, Hallasan and the Geomunoreum lava tubes, have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.** The Seongsan Ilchulbong summit trail costs ₩5,000 for adults; the coastal walking area is free. Reaching the top of Hallasan, South Korea's highest mountain, takes a reservation, ID that matches it and an early start: summit-route checkpoints close at 11:30 (October–March) or 12:30 (April–September). Adult fares by transit card are ₩1,150 on regular buses, including tourist circular buses, while express buses start at ₩2,000 and cost up to ₩3,000 depending on distance.

Below: each sight in a table, Hallasan rules, buses, food and a two-day plan.

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110731), [Hallasan National Park](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/board/boardView.do?bbsId=notice&seq=1270) and [Jeju Bus Information System](https://bus.jeju.go.kr/mobile/schedule/busfare); checked Oct 23, 2026.

![Graphic: Jeju at a glance — UNESCO volcanic island, Seongsan Ilchulbong, Hallasan reservation, buses, black pork](/img/jeju-steps.png?v=a3fc4668 "Jeju at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Why go | Volcanic landscapes listed by UNESCO (2007), plus the haenyeo diving culture |
| Seongsan Ilchulbong | Adults ₩5,000 for the summit trail; closed on the first Monday of the month (or the next day if that Monday is a holiday) |
| Hallasan summit | Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails: reservation and ID needed |
| Buses | Regular buses ₩1,150 by card; express buses from ₩2,000 |
| Must-eat | Heukdwaeji (Jeju black pork) with *meljeot* anchovy sauce |
| Emergencies | 119 (fire and ambulance), 112 (police) |

Source: [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110731), [Hallasan National Park](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/), [Jeju Bus Information System](https://bus.jeju.go.kr/mobile/schedule/busfare) and [Visit Jeju](https://www.visitjeju.net/en/detail/view?contentsid=CNTS_300000000012875); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Why Jeju matters

In 2007, UNESCO listed **Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes** as a World Heritage Site. It has three parts:

| Part | What UNESCO says |
|---|---|
| **Seongsan Ilchulbong** | A "fortress-like" tuff cone rising out of the ocean |
| **Mount Halla (Hallasan)** | "The highest in Korea," with a lake-filled crater at the top |
| **Geomunoreum** | "The finest lava tube system of caves anywhere" |

Jeju is also known for its **haenyeo**, women divers who gather shellfish such as abalone and sea urchins without oxygen masks. UNESCO added the Culture of Jeju Haenyeo to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2016.

Source: [UNESCO — Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1264) and [Culture of Jeju Haenyeo](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/culture-of-jeju-haenyeo-women-divers-01068); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Seongsan Ilchulbong

![Seongsan Ilchulbong's green slopes and cliffs at blue hour, with blue hydrangeas in the foreground](/img/photo-jeju-seongsan.jpg?v=b08a67a6 "Seongsan Ilchulbong with hydrangeas, June 2024. Photo: Basile Morin (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Seongsan Ilchulbong rose 180 meters out of the sea more than 5,000 years ago and was once a separate island. The crater at the top is about 600 meters across and 90 meters deep. From the summit you can see Udo Island and watch the sunrise.

| | |
|---|---|
| Admission | Adults ₩5,000 · teenagers and children ₩2,500 (paid summit trail) |
| Free option | A free walking trail around the base and coast |
| Climb | About 30–40 minutes to the summit, on stairs and slopes |
| Closed | First Monday of the month (the next day if that Monday is a holiday) |
| Parking | Free |

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Seongsan Ilchulbong Tuff Cone](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110731) and [Visit Jeju — Seongsan Ilchulbong](https://www.visitjeju.net/kr/detail/view?contentsid=cont_000000000500349); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Opening hours vary by season. Before a sunrise visit, check the current opening, last-entry and closing information on [Visit Jeju's Seongsan Ilchulbong page](https://www.visitjeju.net/kr/detail/view?contentsid=cont_000000000500349).

## Hiking Hallasan

![Snow-covered Baengnokdam crater at the summit of Hallasan under a blue sky](/img/photo-jeju-hallasan.jpg?v=329a2768 "Baengnokdam, the crater at the top of Hallasan, January 2025. Photo: Sadopaul (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

The two trails that reach the summit, **Seongpanak** and **Gwaneumsa**, run on a reservation system, and you can only enter at your booked time.

| | Summit trails (Seongpanak, Gwaneumsa) |
|---|---|
| Book | [visithalla.jeju.go.kr](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/) (English menu) · bookings for a month open at 09:00 Korea time on the first business day of the month before |
| Your ticket | Entry and exit QR codes, sent to the phone number you enter |
| Bring | ID that matches your booking details, plus your QR code |
| Earliest entry | 05:00 |
| Uphill cutoff | 11:30 (October–March) · 12:30 (April–September) at the trail entrance **and** at the summit-route checkpoints (Jindallaebat on Seongpanak, Samgakbong on Gwaneumsa) |
| Leave the summit by | 13:30 (October–March) · 14:30 (April–September) |
| Weather | Trails close partly or fully during heavy rain, strong wind, typhoon or heavy snow warnings |

**Don't treat the cutoff as a starting time.** The checkpoints are well up the trail, so book an early entry slot and give yourself enough time to reach them.

**Rules that can cost you a booking:**

- If you don't cancel and don't show up, you can't book for 3 months (1 year for a second no-show).
- If your ID doesn't match your QR details, you can be refused entry and banned from booking for 1 year. Reselling QR codes is not allowed.

Source: Hallasan National Park — [reservation system](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/), [reservation guide](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/contents/contents.do?id=49), [entry and descent time limits](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/board/boardView.do?bbsId=notice&seq=1270) and [ID check notice](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/board/boardView.do?bbsId=notice&seq=1295); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Drinking alcohol and smoking are prohibited in the park, and disposable lunch boxes aren't allowed in. Gimbap and burgers are fine, according to the park's own guide.

## Getting around by bus

Jeju's buses reach most of the island, and Visit Jeju recommends a transportation card such as T-money (see our [T-money guide](/how-to-get-t-money-card-korea/)).

| Bus | Adult fare by card |
|---|---|
| Regular buses (including tourist circular buses) | ₩1,150 (₩1,200 in cash) |
| Express buses | ₩2,000 for the first 20 km, up to ₩3,000 |

On express buses, tap your card again when you get off: the rest of the fare for the distance you rode is charged then. Plan each route in [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/).

Source: [Jeju Bus Information System — fares](https://bus.jeju.go.kr/mobile/schedule/busfare) and [Visit Jeju — Public Transportation in Jeju](https://www.visitjeju.net/en/themtour/view?contentsid=CNTS_200000000012534); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What to eat

| | |
|---|---|
| Dish | **Heukdwaeji** (Jeju black pork), which Visit Jeju calls one of the island's representative foods |
| How it's eaten | Grilled and dipped in **meljeot**, a Jeju-style fermented anchovy sauce |
| Where | Black Pork Street in Jeju City (26 Gwandeok-ro 15-gil), lined with restaurants that specialize in it |

Source: [Visit Jeju — Heukdwaeji (Black Pork)](https://www.visitjeju.net/en/detail/view?contentsid=CNTS_300000000012875); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Many black pork restaurants also serve ordinary pork, so Visit Jeju suggests checking that what you order is heukdwaeji.

## A two-day plan

> **Our take:** Give Jeju at least two days. Bus rides across the island take time, so group nearby sights together.

| Day | Where |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | East side: Seongsan Ilchulbong (summit or the free coastal trail) |
| Day 2 | Hallasan, if you've booked the summit: start at your early entry slot |
| Evening | Black pork in Jeju City |

## Before you go

1. Book your flight to Jeju International Airport.
2. Hiking to the top of Hallasan? Reserve at visithalla.jeju.go.kr as soon as bookings open, and pack ID that matches your booking.
3. Bring a transit card such as T-money for the buses.
4. Install Naver Map to plan bus routes.
5. Check Seongsan Ilchulbong's closing day for your month (first Monday, or the next day after a Monday holiday).
6. Save the emergency numbers: 119 and 112.

Source: [Hallasan National Park](https://visithalla.jeju.go.kr/board/boardView.do?bbsId=notice&seq=1295), [Korea Tourism Organization](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110731) and [Visit Jeju](https://www.visitjeju.net/en/themtour/view?contentsid=CNTS_000000000022574); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### Do I need a reservation to hike Hallasan?

To reach the summit, yes. The Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails run on reservations at visithalla.jeju.go.kr. You can only enter at your booked time, and you need ID that matches your booking.

### What time do I have to start the Hallasan summit hike?

Entry opens at 05:00. Hikers heading for the summit must pass the trail entrance and the summit-route checkpoint (Jindallaebat or Samgakbong) by 11:30 from October to March, or 12:30 from April to September, so start well before that.

### How much is Seongsan Ilchulbong?

₩5,000 for adults and ₩2,500 for teenagers and children for the summit trail. There's also a free coastal trail. It's closed on the first Monday of each month, or the next day if that Monday is a holiday.

### How much is the bus in Jeju?

₩1,150 on regular buses with a transit card. Express buses start at ₩2,000 and go up to ₩3,000 depending on distance.

### What food is Jeju famous for?

Heukdwaeji, Jeju black pork, usually grilled and dipped in meljeot anchovy sauce.

# Jeonju Day Trip from Seoul: Hanok Village Guide

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/jeonju-day-trip-from-seoul/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- Take the KTX from Yongsan Station. Seoul to Jeonju takes about 1 hour 40 minutes, and Yongsan has more Jeonju trains than Seoul Station. A standard-class adult fare example is ₩31,600 via Gongju; fares vary by route.
- Jeonju Hanok Village is free to enter and open all year. It's a historic neighborhood of around 700 hanok buildings, with Gyeonggijeon Shrine (adults aged 25–64 ₩3,000) at its heart.
- Book ahead for weekends. Jeonju's tourism office says KTX seats sell out quickly on weekends, holidays and festival seasons.

**Jeonju is about 1 hour 40 minutes from Seoul by KTX from Yongsan Station (a standard-class adult fare example is ₩31,600 via Gongju; fares and journey times vary by service), and Yongsan has more Jeonju trains than Seoul Station.** Jeonju Hanok Village is free to enter and open all year, with around 700 hanok buildings, and Gyeonggijeon Shrine costs ₩3,000 for adults aged 25–64 (free for everyone on the last Wednesday of each month). On weekends and holidays, book early: Jeonju's tourism office says KTX seats sell out quickly.

Source: [Visit Jeonju — getting to Jeonju](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205008000000), [Korea Tourism Organization — Jeonju Hanok Village](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110848) and [Gyeonggijeon Shrine](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=108728), and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026); checked Oct 23, 2026.

![Graphic: Jeonju day trip at a glance — KTX from Yongsan, Hanok Village, Gyeonggijeon Shrine, what to eat](/img/jeonju-steps.png?v=d3ebdb62 "Jeonju day trip at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What to know |
|---|---|
| Train | KTX from Yongsan Station, about 1 hour 40 minutes on faster services; fare example ₩31,600 via Gongju (standard adult), varies by route |
| From the airport | Direct airport bus from Incheon to Jeonju (different arrival point from the train) |
| Hanok Village | Free to enter, open all year, around 700 hanok buildings |
| Gyeonggijeon Shrine | Adults (25–64) ₩3,000; free for everyone on the last Wednesday of each month |
| Busy times | Weekends, holidays and festival seasons: book seats early |

Source: [Visit Jeonju — getting to Jeonju](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205008000000), [Korea Tourism Organization — Jeonju Hanok Village](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110848) and [Gyeonggijeon Shrine](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=108728), and Korail's KTX fare table (as of Sep 1, 2026; see our [KTX guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/)); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Getting there

**By KTX (fastest).** Jeonju's tourism office puts the KTX at about 1 hour 40 minutes from Seoul, and it points out that Jeonju trains leave Yongsan Station much more often than Seoul Station. If Seoul Station looks sold out, search from Yongsan. Korail's fare table lists a standard-class adult fare of ₩31,600 from Yongsan to Jeonju via Gongju and ₩31,000 via Seodaejeon. Check the route, travel time and final fare for your chosen train. Our [KTX booking guide](/how-to-book-ktx-korea/) walks through buying tickets in English.

**From Incheon Airport.** If you're heading straight to Jeonju after landing, there's a direct airport bus. Tickets are sold at the counters and kiosks in the arrivals area, and the kiosks take overseas credit cards. For Daehan Limousine's buses to the Jeonju Limousine Terminal, the operator lists boarding at zone 12B at Terminal 1 and zone 9 at Terminal 2. Buses sold as "Jeonju" can stop at different places in the city, so check the operator and arrival terminal on your ticket and follow the bay printed on it. The tourism office suggests picking a bus at least 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours after your landing time, to allow for immigration and baggage.

**Know where you'll arrive.** Jeonju Station (trains), the Jeonju Limousine Terminal (airport buses) and the express and intercity bus terminals are all in different places. Put your exact arrival point and "Jeonju Hanok Village" into [Naver Map](/how-to-use-naver-map-korea/) to see the current bus or taxi route from there.

Source: [Visit Jeonju — getting to Jeonju](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205008000000), [Daehan Limousine — boarding locations](http://www.limusine.co.kr/sub/sub02) (Korean); KTX fare from Korail's fare table as of Sep 1, 2026; checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** For a weekend or holiday trip, buy your KTX seats as soon as you know your date. Jeonju's tourism office warns that on busy days the station often has only standing-room tickets left.

## Jeonju Hanok Village

![Grey tiled hanok roofs of Jeonju Hanok Village, with the modern city behind](/img/photo-jeonju-hanok-rooftops.jpg?v=9a65e9f8 "Rooftops of Jeonju Hanok Village, April 2023. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Jeonju Hanok Village is a large historic neighborhood in the city, with around 700 hanok buildings according to the Korea Tourism Organization. It grew from the early 1900s around Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Omokdae and the Jeonju Hyanggyo Confucian academy. Entry is free and it's open all year.

Most of the day is simply walking the lanes. The village also offers traditional performances, crafts and games, and hanbok rental is easy to find: the tourism organization notes there are many rental shops near Gyeonggijeon. To see a hanok from the inside, you can stay overnight in a hanok guesthouse or visit the Hanok Life Experience Hall.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Jeonju Hanok Village](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110848); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Gyeonggijeon Shrine

![The red gate and stone path leading into Gyeonggijeon Shrine in Jeonju](/img/photo-jeonju-gyeonggijeon.jpg?v=5f4e9e9a "Gyeonggijeon Shrine, Jeonju, April 2023. Photo: Mobius6 (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.")

Gyeonggijeon sits inside the village. It was founded in 1410 and holds the portrait of King Taejo, the founder of the Joseon dynasty. Inside the grounds is Jeonju Sago, one of the four repositories for the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty, and the only one whose copy survived the Imjin War (1592–1598). Your shrine ticket covers it.

Admission is ₩3,000 for adults (25–64), ₩2,000 for ages 13–24 and ₩1,000 for children aged 7–12. Everyone gets in free on the last Wednesday of every month, and children aged 6 and under are always free. Jeonju City's own guide lists the free entry for people 65 and over as being for Korean nationals, so older overseas visitors shouldn't assume age alone makes it free; ask at the ticket office.

Opening hours change with the seasons: 09:00–19:00 from March to May and in September and October, 09:00–20:00 from June to August, and 09:00–18:00 from November to February. The last entry is one hour before closing. The Korea Tourism Organization suggests pairing it with Jeondong Cathedral nearby.

Source: [Korea Tourism Organization — Gyeonggijeon Shrine](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=108728), [Jeonju Hanok Village — Gyeonggijeon](https://hanok.jeonju.go.kr/contents/place) (Korean) and [Visit Jeonju — Jeonju Sago](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/board/view.jeonju?boardId=BBS_0000016&menuCd=DOM_000000201005001000&paging=ok&startPage=1&dataSid=16782); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Getting around the village

The village is compact enough to walk. Jeonju also runs a free shuttle all year, mainly for people who park, connecting Hanok Village Public Parking Lot No. 4 with the village. On weekdays one bus makes 16 runs; on weekends and holidays it runs frequently from 10:00 to 18:30.

Source: [Visit Jeonju — shuttle bus](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205012000000); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What to eat

Jeonju is a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, and bibimbap is its signature. We cover the dishes, the markets and where to find them in [what to eat in Jeonju](/what-to-eat-in-jeonju/).

> **Our take:** A simple day plan works best. Take a morning KTX from Yongsan, see Gyeonggijeon first, then wander the village and eat. Leave buffer time for your return train, especially on a weekend.

## Before you go

1. Book your KTX from Yongsan, early if it's a weekend or holiday.
2. Check which Jeonju arrival point you're using (station or bus terminal).
3. Install Naver Map for the route from there to the village.
4. Bring a little cash and a card; see [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).
5. Note Gyeonggijeon's seasonal hours (last entry one hour before closing).

Source: [Visit Jeonju — getting to Jeonju](https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205008000000) and [Korea Tourism Organization — Gyeonggijeon Shrine](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=108728); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### How do I get from Seoul to Jeonju?

The KTX is fastest: about 1 hour 40 minutes, with more departures from Yongsan Station than from Seoul Station. A standard-class adult fare example from Yongsan is ₩31,600 via Gongju; fares vary by route. There's also a direct airport bus from Incheon.

### Is Jeonju Hanok Village free?

Yes. The village is free to enter and open all year. Some sights inside charge admission, such as Gyeonggijeon Shrine (₩3,000 for adults aged 25–64).

### Is a day trip to Jeonju enough?

In our view, a full day covers the Hanok Village, Gyeonggijeon and a couple of meals. If you'd like to stay in a hanok, Jeonju has hanok guesthouses for an overnight stay.

### When is Gyeonggijeon free?

On the last Wednesday of every month, for everyone. Children aged 6 and under are always free. The free entry for people 65 and over is listed for Korean nationals, so overseas seniors should check at the ticket office.

## Sources

- Visit Jeonju (Jeonju City) — Getting to Jeonju: https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205008000000
- Visit Jeonju — Free Hanok Village shuttle bus: https://tour.jeonju.go.kr/eng/index.jeonju?menuCd=DOM_000000205012000000
- Korea Tourism Organization — Jeonju Hanok Village: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=110848
- Korea Tourism Organization — Gyeonggijeon Shrine: https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/whereToGo/locIntrdn/rgnContentsView.do?vcontsId=108728
- Jeonju Hanok Village (Jeonju City) — Gyeonggijeon hours and admission (Korean): https://hanok.jeonju.go.kr/contents/place

# K-ETA Explained: Do You Need One to Visit Korea?

URL: https://realkoreatrip.com/k-eta-korea/
Last checked: 2026-10-23

## Quick answer

- K-ETA is an online travel authorization for people who can enter Korea without a visa. Where it's required, you need approval before you board your flight or ship.
- 22 countries and regions are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (Korea time), including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia. Check the official list, then confirm on the K-ETA site.
- Apply only on the official site (k-eta.go.kr) or the K-ETA app. The fee is ₩10,000 (about US$7–8, plus a separate online payment fee), and approval usually takes up to 72 hours.

**If you can enter Korea without a visa, you normally need a K-ETA before you board, but 22 countries and regions, including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia, are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (Korea time).** Some travelers are also exempt personally (see below). If you do need one, apply only on k-eta.go.kr or the official K-ETA app: the fee is ₩10,000 (about US$7–8, plus a separate online payment fee), processing typically takes 72 hours or less, and it's valid for 3 years or until your passport expires, if that's sooner.

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [exemption notice](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y); checked Oct 23, 2026.

![Graphic: K-ETA in brief — who it's for, the temporary exemption until December 31, 2026, the fee and processing time](/img/keta-facts.png?v=0f511aef "K-ETA at a glance. Details and sources below.")

## The short version

| | What the official site says |
|---|---|
| Who it's for | People who can enter Korea without a visa, visiting short-term for travel, family, events or business (no commercial activities) |
| When you need it | Before you board your flight or ship to Korea |
| Temporary exemption | 22 countries and regions don't need it until December 31, 2026 (KST) |
| Fee | ₩10,000 (about US$7–8), plus a separate online payment fee — not refunded if refused |
| Processing time | Typically 72 hours or less; no paid fast track |
| Valid for | 3 years, or until your passport expires if that's sooner |
| Where to apply | k-eta.go.kr or the official K-ETA app |

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do), [eligible countries](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do) and [exemption notice](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## What K-ETA is (and isn't)

K-ETA is Korea's Electronic Travel Authorization. It's for travelers from countries and regions whose citizens can enter Korea without a visa. Where it applies, you need approval before you board your flight or ship — the official guide warns that applying after boarding, or once you're already in Korea, can lead to refusal or entry restrictions.

It isn't a visa. The site is clear that an approved K-ETA doesn't guarantee entry: the final decision is made by an immigration officer when you arrive. And it doesn't change how long you can stay. The K-ETA validity is separate from your visa-free stay — for example, the official list shows 90 days for US citizens and 6 months for Canadians.

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [eligible countries](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## The temporary exemption, until December 31, 2026

Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended a temporary K-ETA exemption for one more year: it runs from January 1 to December 31, 2026 (Korea time) and applies to the countries and regions that were already exempt.

The extension notice itself doesn't list the countries, but the Korea Tourism Organization publishes the list of 22 countries and regions covered through December 31, 2026:

- **Asia:** Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macau
- **North America:** United States (including Guam), Canada
- **Europe:** United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Spain, Poland, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Belgium, Denmark, Austria
- **Oceania:** Australia, New Zealand

Check that official list, and confirm your own status on the K-ETA site before you travel: if you're exempt, you'll see a pop-up message when you scan the photo page of your passport during the application.

Even if you're exempt, you can still choose to apply — the notice mentions benefits such as not having to fill in an arrival card. In that case you pay the fee, and it isn't refunded. The temporary K-ETA exemption alone does not exempt you from the arrival card. If you travel without a valid K-ETA, [check whether you need to submit an e-Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); other exemptions, such as holding a valid Korean Residence Card, may apply. The official service is free.

Source: [K-ETA — notice on extension of temporary exemption](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y) (posted Dec 23, 2025), [Korea Tourism Organization — visa & travel requirements](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769) (updated Sep 18, 2026) and [e-Arrival Card — who needs to submit](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Our take:** If you'll be entering Korea in 2027, check the latest official notice before you travel. The extension notice cited here confirms the temporary exemption only through December 31, 2026 (KST).

## Who doesn't need to apply

The official FAQ lists people who are exempt from applying, including:

- Holders of a valid Korean passport (including dual nationals)
- Registered foreigners and people with a Korean visa
- Children aged 17 and under, and adults aged 65 and over, on the date of entry
- Transfer passengers — unless you need to enter Korea because of an itinerary change or to collect your baggage
- Cruise travelers
- Flight attendants and seafarers, ABTC (APEC) card holders, UN passport holders, diplomatic and official passport holders, and active-duty US service members under the US–Korea SOFA

Source: [K-ETA — FAQ, "Who is eligible for the application exemption?"](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboardlist.do?tmpltNm=faq2); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## How to apply

![The arrivals hall of Incheon Airport Terminal 1, seen from the floor above](/img/photo-icn-t1-arrivals.jpg?v=66c8964f "Incheon Airport Terminal 1 arrivals hall, 2023. Photo: ノボホショコロトソ (CC BY 4.0), cropped.")

Have these ready: a valid passport, an email address you can check, an ID photo, and a credit or debit card for the fee. Then:

1. Go to **k-eta.go.kr** (or the official K-ETA app) and choose to apply as a member or a non-member.
2. Enter your passport details — this is the point where exempt travelers see the pop-up.
3. Enter your travel details, check everything, and pay the ₩10,000 fee.
4. Wait for the result. The site says it typically takes 72 hours or less, but it can take longer when applications spike, and there's no expedited service.

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN), [application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [what to prepare](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

> **Local tip:** Apply well before your flight rather than counting on the 72-hour figure, and make sure the details you enter match your passport exactly. The site warns that false or inaccurate information can get an approval refused or cancelled.

## Watch out for fake K-ETA sites

The official site carries a warning about look-alike agencies and phishing sites that charge high fees for "agency" or "expedited" K-ETA applications. The site says applications are accepted only at www.k-eta.go.kr or through the K-ETA mobile app, and it offers no paid fast track.

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN) and [application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## After you're approved

- **Use it again.** A K-ETA can be used for multiple trips during its 3-year validity (or until your passport expires, if sooner).
- **Skip the arrival card — when you enter on your K-ETA.** If you also hold a Korean visa and enter on that visa, the official [e-Arrival Card guide](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do) says you must complete an e-Arrival Card.
- **New passport, new K-ETA.** If your passport is reissued — or your criminal record or infectious disease information changes — you need to apply again.
- **Keep your travel details up to date.** If your purpose of visit, address in Korea, contact details, travel dates or companions change, update them on the official site.

Source: [K-ETA — application guide](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do) and [e-Arrival Card — who needs to submit](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## Before you fly

1. Check the [official exempt list](https://english.visitkorea.or.kr/svc/contents/contentsView.do?vcontsId=140769), then confirm on k-eta.go.kr — scan your passport and see if the exemption pop-up appears.
2. Using the temporary exemption without a valid K-ETA? [Check whether you need to submit the free e-Arrival Card](https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do), unless another arrival-card exemption applies.
3. If you need a K-ETA, apply on the official site or app and pay ₩10,000.
4. Allow time for processing before your flight.
5. Plan your arrival: [Incheon Airport to Seoul](/incheon-airport-to-seoul/), [getting online](/esim-sim-card-pocket-wifi-korea/) and [paying in Korea](/paying-in-korea-foreign-cards-cash/).

Source: [K-ETA — official website](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN) and [exemption notice](https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y); checked Oct 23, 2026.

## FAQ

### Do I need a K-ETA to visit Korea in 2026?

It depends on your passport. K-ETA is for people who can enter Korea without a visa, but 22 countries and regions — including the US, Canada, the UK, Japan and Australia — are temporarily exempt until December 31, 2026 (KST). The K-ETA site shows a pop-up if you're exempt when you scan your passport.

### How much does a K-ETA cost?

₩10,000 (about US$7–8), plus a separate online payment fee. It isn't refunded if your application is refused.

### How long does K-ETA approval take?

The official site says typically 72 hours or less, though it can take longer. There's no expedited service.

### How long is a K-ETA valid?

3 years, or until your passport expires if that's sooner. You can use it for multiple trips, but each stay is still limited to your visa-free period.

### Do children need a K-ETA?

Children aged 17 and under on the date of entry are on the official list of people exempt from applying, as are adults aged 65 and over.

## Sources

- K-ETA (Ministry of Justice) — official website: https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/newapply/index.do?locale=EN
- K-ETA — Application guide (fee, processing time, validity): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaapplication.do
- K-ETA — Eligible countries and what to prepare: https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/guide/viewetaalification.do
- K-ETA — Notice on extension of K-ETA temporary exemption (Dec 23, 2025): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboarddetail.do?bbsSn=299707&esntlPnotiMtYn=Y
- K-ETA — FAQ (who is exempt from applying): https://www.k-eta.go.kr/portal/board/viewboardlist.do?tmpltNm=faq2

- e-Arrival Card (Ministry of Justice) — who needs to submit: https://www.e-arrivalcard.go.kr/portal/guide/eacTargetGuide.do
